CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Oogenesis is the process of forming ova.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: The release of a secondary oocyte from a mature ovarian follicle is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Ovulation releases a secondary oocyte from the ovary.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which structure forms from the ruptured follicle after ovulation?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The corpus luteum secretes progesterone.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Where does fertilisation normally occur in humans?
options: Ampullary-isthmic region of the uterine tube
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Human fertilisation normally occurs at the ampullary-isthmic junction of the oviduct.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: The attachment of the blastocyst to the uterine endometrium is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Implantation embeds the blastocyst in the uterine lining.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which temporary organ facilitates exchange between maternal and foetal blood systems?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The placenta supports exchange and also functions as an endocrine tissue.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which hormone primarily stimulates milk production after childbirth?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Prolactin stimulates milk synthesis; oxytocin helps milk ejection.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: What is the main purpose of contraceptive methods?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Contraception helps prevent unintended pregnancy.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which barrier method can also reduce transmission risk of many sexually transmitted infections?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Correct condom use reduces pregnancy and STI transmission risk.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Copper-releasing intrauterine devices are primarily used to prevent what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Copper IUDs interfere with sperm function and reduce the chance of fertilisation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: In which assisted reproductive technique is fertilisation initiated outside the body?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: IVF involves fertilising an oocyte outside the body before embryo transfer.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which surgical procedure is a method of male sterilisation?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Vasectomy blocks or cuts the vas deferens.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which surgical procedure is a method of female sterilisation?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Tubectomy blocks or cuts the fallopian tubes.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which action helps reduce the risk of sexually transmitted infections?
options: Correct condom use and appropriate testing
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Prevention includes barrier protection, testing and timely medical care.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Amniocentesis involves sampling which fluid for certain prenatal tests?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Amniotic fluid may contain foetal cells useful for selected diagnostic tests.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: What is the most appropriate next step when a couple has concerns about infertility?
options: Seek assessment from a qualified healthcare professional
Assume one partner is always responsible
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Infertility may have multiple causes and should be evaluated appropriately.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which technique involves placing processed semen into the female reproductive tract?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Artificial insemination introduces semen into the reproductive tract by a medical procedure.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: A gene is best described as what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Genes are DNA sequences that contribute to functional products and inherited traits.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Alternative forms of the same gene are called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Alleles occupy corresponding loci and can contribute to variation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: The genetic constitution of an organism for a trait is its what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Genotype refers to genetic makeup.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: The observable characteristics of an organism are called its what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Phenotype reflects genotype and environmental influences.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which ABO blood group phenotype expresses both A and B antigens on red blood cells?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The AB phenotype expresses both A and B antigens.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: In the human ABO blood group system, IA and IB alleles show what relationship?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Both IA and IB are expressed in the AB phenotype.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: A gene with more than two alternative forms in a population is said to have what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: A population may contain multiple alleles, though a diploid individual carries at most two.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: The Rh-positive phenotype commonly reflects the presence of which red-cell antigen?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The D antigen is the major antigen used in routine Rh classification.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: A heritable change in DNA sequence is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Mutations can create new genetic variants.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which chart is used to trace inheritance of a trait through family generations?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Pedigree charts help analyse inheritance patterns in families.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which molecule is the principal hereditary material in most organisms?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: DNA stores hereditary information in most organisms.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which components make up a nucleotide?
options: Amino acid and fatty acid only
Sugar, phosphate group and nitrogenous base
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: A nucleotide consists of a pentose sugar, phosphate group and nitrogenous base.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which base pairs with adenine in DNA?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which nitrogenous base occurs in RNA in place of thymine?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: RNA typically contains uracil instead of thymine.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Why is DNA replication described as semiconservative?
options: Each daughter molecule contains one parental and one newly synthesised strand
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Each daughter double helix retains one original strand.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: The synthesis of RNA using DNA as a template is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Transcription produces RNA from a DNA template.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: The process by which ribosomes use mRNA to synthesise a polypeptide is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Translation converts mRNA codon information into an amino-acid sequence.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: A sequence of three nucleotides in mRNA that specifies an amino acid or stop signal is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Codons are read in triplets during translation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which RNA molecule carries amino acids to the ribosome?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: tRNA carries amino acids and pairs its anticodon with an mRNA codon.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: DNA fingerprinting commonly compares which type of variation?
options: Variable DNA regions such as STRs
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Variable DNA markers can help distinguish individuals.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Natural selection acts on heritable variation that affects what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Individuals with advantageous heritable traits may leave more offspring.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: A heritable feature that improves reproductive success in a particular environment is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Adaptations can increase fitness in a given environment.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, what is the relationship between allele frequencies p and q for a two-allele locus?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: For two alleles, their frequencies sum to one.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Random changes in allele frequencies are especially influential in which populations?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Sampling effects can cause strong random changes in small populations.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Movement of alleles between populations through migration and reproduction is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Gene flow transfers genetic variants between populations.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Fossils provide evidence about what?
options: Past life and changes through geological time
Exact genotype of every living organism
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Fossils document organisms and evolutionary changes across geological time.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Structures with a common evolutionary origin but possibly different functions are called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Homologous structures support common ancestry.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Structures that perform similar functions but evolved independently are called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Analogy often results from convergent evolution.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: The formation of new species is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Speciation occurs when populations diverge and become reproductively isolated.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: The spread of antibiotic resistance in bacteria is an example of evolution by what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Antibiotics select for resistant variants.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: An organism or agent that can cause disease is called a what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Pathogens include certain bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Malaria is caused by which genus of protozoan parasites?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Plasmodium species cause malaria.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Malaria is transmitted by the bite of an infected female mosquito of which genus?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Dengue is caused by which type of pathogen?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Dengue is caused by dengue viruses.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Tuberculosis is caused by which organism?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which cells differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Activated B cells can differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Vaccination primarily aims to generate what?
options: Immediate replacement of all white cells
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Vaccines stimulate immune responses and memory against specific pathogens.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Cancer is characterised by abnormal, uncontrolled what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Cancer involves uncontrolled cell growth and may invade other tissues.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: HIV primarily attacks which immune cells?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: HIV targets CD4-positive immune cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: An exaggerated immune response to a normally harmless substance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Allergies are hypersensitivity responses to specific allergens.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which microbes help convert milk into curd?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Lactic acid bacteria ferment lactose and acidify milk.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which microorganism is widely used in bread-making and alcoholic fermentation?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Yeast ferments sugars under suitable conditions.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Penicillin was discovered from a mould belonging to which genus?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Penicillium moulds produce penicillin compounds.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which microorganisms produce methane under anaerobic conditions in biogas plants?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Methanogens generate methane in anaerobic digesters.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Activated sludge treatment relies heavily on what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Microorganisms break down organic pollutants in wastewater.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Rhizobium bacteria commonly form nitrogen-fixing associations with which plants?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Rhizobium in legume root nodules fixes atmospheric nitrogen.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Mycorrhiza is an association between plant roots and what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Mycorrhizal fungi can improve uptake of minerals.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Using living organisms to manage pests is known as what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Biological control uses natural enemies or antagonists to reduce pests.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Biochemical oxygen demand is used as an indicator of what in water?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Higher BOD generally indicates greater oxygen demand from biodegradable matter.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Antibiotics are primarily used against susceptible infections caused by what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Antibiotics act against bacteria and do not directly treat viral infections.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific DNA sequences and do what?
options: Cut DNA at or near those sequences
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sites.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which enzyme joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: What is the main purpose of polymerase chain reaction?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: PCR produces many copies of a target DNA segment.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: A small circular DNA molecule often used as a cloning vector is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Plasmids can carry inserted DNA into host cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Why are selectable markers used in cloning vectors?
options: To identify or select cells carrying the vector
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Selectable markers help distinguish transformed cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: A bioreactor provides controlled conditions for what?
options: Biological production using cells or enzymes
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Bioreactors control pH, temperature, aeration and other conditions.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: DNA fragments are separated during agarose gel electrophoresis mainly according to what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Smaller DNA fragments usually move farther through agarose gel.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: DNA formed by joining genetic material from different sources is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Recombinant DNA combines sequences from different sources.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which vector feature allows DNA replication to begin in a host cell?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The origin of replication is where replication machinery initiates copying.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: In genetic engineering, competent cells are capable of doing what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Competent cells are prepared to take up DNA.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Bt cotton contains genes derived from which bacterium?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Bt genes can enable plants to produce proteins toxic to certain insect pests.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: RNA interference can silence gene expression through which type of molecule?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: RNA interference uses small RNA molecules to reduce specific RNA transcripts.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Gene therapy aims to treat disease by introducing or modifying what?
options: Genetic material or gene function in cells
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Gene therapy seeks to alter gene function or expression.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Recombinant human insulin can be produced using which general technology?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Recombinant DNA methods enable microbes to produce human insulin.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: An organism carrying introduced genetic material is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Transgenic organisms contain introduced genetic material.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: ELISA commonly detects a target using specific binding between antigen and what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: ELISA uses antigen-antibody recognition and an enzyme-linked signal.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: PCR can help diagnose some infections by detecting what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: PCR amplifies pathogen-specific nucleic acid targets.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Why is biosafety assessment important before releasing a genetically modified organism?
options: To assess potential risks to health and the environment
To guarantee zero risk without testing
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Risk assessment evaluates potential hazards and exposure pathways.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Golden rice was developed to increase which nutrient precursor in rice endosperm?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Golden rice is engineered to accumulate beta-carotene, a provitamin A carotenoid.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: A patent related to a biological invention or process is commonly called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Biopatents concern qualifying biological inventions subject to applicable law.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: A population consists of individuals of the same species living in what context?
options: The same area at the same time
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Population ecology studies members of a species sharing an area and time.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: The place where an organism lives is called its what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Habitat refers to the physical place an organism occupies.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: The ecological role and resource use of a species are described by its what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: A niche describes how a species uses resources and interacts with its environment.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: The maximum population size an environment can sustain over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Carrying capacity depends on resources and environmental conditions.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Under ideal conditions with unlimited resources, population growth may form which curve?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Exponential growth accelerates when limiting factors are absent.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Population growth that slows as it approaches carrying capacity is represented by which curve?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Logistic growth includes density-dependent limitation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: In mutualism, how are the two species affected?
options: One benefits and the other is always harmed
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Mutualism is an interaction in which both partners benefit.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: In parasitism, which organism benefits while the other is harmed?
options: Parasite benefits and host is harmed
Host benefits and parasite is harmed
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Parasites obtain resources from hosts, often causing harm.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: In commensalism, what is the typical relationship?
options: One species benefits while the other is not significantly affected
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Commensalism benefits one species without a major effect on the other.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: In predation, the predator generally does what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Predators obtain food by capturing or consuming prey.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: An ecosystem includes a community of organisms and what else?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: An ecosystem includes living organisms and their physical environment.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which organisms form the first trophic level in most ecosystems?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Producers capture energy, commonly through photosynthesis.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which organisms break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Fungi and bacteria commonly act as decomposers.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Energy flow through an ecosystem is generally what?
options: Unidirectional, with energy lost as heat at each transfer
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Energy dissipates as heat and is not recycled like nutrients.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Lindeman's ten percent law describes approximately how much energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Only a small fraction, often approximated as 10%, passes to the next trophic level.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which ecological pyramid is always upright?
options: Pyramid of biomass in every case
Pyramid of numbers in every case
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Energy decreases at successive trophic levels.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Primary productivity refers to the rate at which producers do what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Primary productivity is the rate of biomass or organic matter production.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which process is part of decomposition?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Decomposition includes fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralisation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: The gradual change in community composition over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Succession describes changes in ecological communities over time.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Unlike energy, nutrients in ecosystems generally do what?
options: Cycle between organisms and the environment
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Elements such as carbon and nitrogen cycle through biotic and abiotic components.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Biodiversity includes variation at genetic, species and what other level?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Biodiversity is considered at genetic, species and ecosystem levels.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: A species naturally restricted to a particular geographic region is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Endemic species have naturally limited geographic distributions.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Protecting species in their natural habitats is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: In situ conservation protects organisms within their natural ecosystems.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which is an example of ex situ conservation?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Seed banks preserve plant genetic material outside its natural habitat.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which organisation publishes the widely used Red List of Threatened Species?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The International Union for Conservation of Nature maintains the Red List.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: A biodiversity hotspot is identified by high endemism and what other feature?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Hotspots combine high endemism with substantial habitat loss.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: A species with a disproportionately large ecological effect relative to its abundance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Keystone species strongly influence ecosystem structure and function.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Breaking a continuous habitat into smaller, isolated patches is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Fragmentation can isolate populations and increase edge effects.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: A species is extinct when what condition is met?
options: It moves to another local habitat
Its population decreases for one season
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Extinction means the species no longer has living individuals.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which action supports long-term biodiversity conservation?
options: Protecting habitats and reducing major threats
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Habitat protection and threat reduction are central conservation measures.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which gas is a major contributor to human-driven global warming?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels and land-use change contribute to warming.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which chemicals historically contributed significantly to stratospheric ozone depletion?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: CFC-derived chlorine radicals can catalyse ozone destruction.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Excess nutrient enrichment of a water body that can cause algal blooms is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus can promote algal growth and oxygen depletion.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: An increase in concentration of persistent pollutants at higher trophic levels is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Persistent pollutants can accumulate through food chains.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Acid rain is mainly associated with atmospheric emissions of which gases?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Sulfur and nitrogen oxides form acids in the atmosphere.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which practice can reduce the amount of waste sent to landfills?
options: Mixing hazardous waste with food waste
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Waste prevention and recovery reduce landfill pressure.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Sound levels are commonly expressed in which unit?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Sound pressure levels are commonly expressed in decibels.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Which is a renewable energy source?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Solar energy is replenished naturally on human timescales.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: The build-up of a substance in an organism over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Bioaccumulation occurs when uptake exceeds elimination.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Establishing forest cover on land not recently forested is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Afforestation establishes tree cover on suitable land.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which type of reproduction usually involves one parent and no fusion of gametes?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Asexual reproduction generally involves one parent and does not involve gamete fusion.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Amoeba commonly reproduces asexually by which method?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: In binary fission, one parent cell divides into two daughter cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which organism commonly reproduces asexually by budding?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Hydra can form a new individual as an outgrowth or bud.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Growing a new plant from a stem cutting is an example of what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Vegetative propagation uses vegetative plant parts to produce new plants.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: The fusion of male and female gametes is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Fertilisation combines the nuclei of compatible gametes.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Development of an individual from an unfertilised egg is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Parthenogenesis is development without fertilisation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Asexual reproductive units produced by many fungi are called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Spores can germinate and develop into new individuals under suitable conditions.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: A group of genetically identical individuals produced asexually is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Asexual reproduction often produces genetically similar or identical offspring.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: In which type of fertilisation do gametes unite outside the body?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: External fertilisation occurs outside the parental body, often in water.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The period from birth to natural death of an organism is called its what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Life span is the duration between birth and natural death.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which part of a typical angiosperm stamen produces pollen grains?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The anther contains microsporangia where pollen grains develop.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: The formation of microspores from pollen mother cells by meiosis is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Microsporogenesis produces haploid microspores by meiosis.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which highly resistant material is found in the exine of pollen grains?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Sporopollenin is highly resistant to chemical and biological degradation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A typical mature angiosperm embryo sac usually has how many cells and nuclei?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The common Polygonum-type embryo sac has seven cells and eight nuclei.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Pollination places pollen on a receptive stigma.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Double fertilisation in angiosperms consists of which two events?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: One male gamete fuses with the egg; the other fuses with the polar nuclei/secondary nucleus.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: In a typical angiosperm, the primary endosperm nucleus is usually what ploidy?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Triple fusion commonly produces a triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Seed formation without fertilisation is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Apomixis can produce seeds without normal fertilisation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Development of a fruit without fertilisation is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Parthenocarpy results in fruit development without fertilisation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which is an example of an outbreeding device in flowering plants?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Dichogamy separates pollen release and stigma receptivity in time.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: The production of sperm cells is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Spermatogenesis occurs in the seminiferous tubules of the testes.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which testicular cells secrete testosterone?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Leydig cells secrete androgens.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which cells support and nourish developing sperm cells in seminiferous tubules?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Sertoli cells support developing germ cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: The formation of female gametes is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Oogenesis is the process of forming ova.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: The release of a secondary oocyte from a mature ovarian follicle is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Ovulation releases a secondary oocyte from the ovary.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which structure forms from the ruptured follicle after ovulation?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The corpus luteum secretes progesterone.

options: Ampullary-isthmic region of the uterine tube
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Human fertilisation normally occurs at the ampullary-isthmic junction of the oviduct.

CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Implantation embeds the blastocyst in the uterine lining.

CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The placenta supports exchange and also functions as an endocrine tissue.

CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Prolactin stimulates milk synthesis; oxytocin helps milk ejection.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: What is the main purpose of contraceptive methods?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Contraception helps prevent unintended pregnancy.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which barrier method can also reduce transmission risk of many sexually transmitted infections?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Correct condom use reduces pregnancy and STI transmission risk.

CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Copper IUDs interfere with sperm function and reduce the chance of fertilisation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.why: IVF involves fertilising an oocyte outside the body before embryo transfer.

options: Correct condom use and appropriate testing
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Prevention includes barrier protection, testing and timely medical care.

CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Amniotic fluid may contain foetal cells useful for selected diagnostic tests.

options: Assume one partner is always responsible
Seek assessment from a qualified healthcare professional
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Infertility may have multiple causes and should be evaluated appropriately.

CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Artificial insemination introduces semen into the reproductive tract by a medical procedure.

CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Genes are DNA sequences that contribute to functional products and inherited traits.

CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Alleles occupy corresponding loci and can contribute to variation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Genotype refers to genetic makeup.
