CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Phenotype reflects genotype and environmental influences.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which ABO blood group phenotype expresses both A and B antigens on red blood cells?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The AB phenotype expresses both A and B antigens.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: In the human ABO blood group system, IA and IB alleles show what relationship?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Both IA and IB are expressed in the AB phenotype.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: A gene with more than two alternative forms in a population is said to have what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: A population may contain multiple alleles, though a diploid individual carries at most two.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: The Rh-positive phenotype commonly reflects the presence of which red-cell antigen?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The D antigen is the major antigen used in routine Rh classification.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: A heritable change in DNA sequence is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Mutations can create new genetic variants.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which chart is used to trace inheritance of a trait through family generations?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Pedigree charts help analyse inheritance patterns in families.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which molecule is the principal hereditary material in most organisms?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: DNA stores hereditary information in most organisms.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which components make up a nucleotide?
options: Sugar, phosphate group and nitrogenous base
Amino acid and fatty acid only
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: A nucleotide consists of a pentose sugar, phosphate group and nitrogenous base.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which base pairs with adenine in DNA?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which nitrogenous base occurs in RNA in place of thymine?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: RNA typically contains uracil instead of thymine.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Why is DNA replication described as semiconservative?
options: Each daughter molecule contains one parental and one newly synthesised strand
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Each daughter double helix retains one original strand.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: The synthesis of RNA using DNA as a template is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Transcription produces RNA from a DNA template.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: The process by which ribosomes use mRNA to synthesise a polypeptide is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Translation converts mRNA codon information into an amino-acid sequence.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A sequence of three nucleotides in mRNA that specifies an amino acid or stop signal is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Codons are read in triplets during translation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which RNA molecule carries amino acids to the ribosome?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: tRNA carries amino acids and pairs its anticodon with an mRNA codon.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: DNA fingerprinting commonly compares which type of variation?
options: Variable DNA regions such as STRs
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Variable DNA markers can help distinguish individuals.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Natural selection acts on heritable variation that affects what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Individuals with advantageous heritable traits may leave more offspring.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A heritable feature that improves reproductive success in a particular environment is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Adaptations can increase fitness in a given environment.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, what is the relationship between allele frequencies p and q for a two-allele locus?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: For two alleles, their frequencies sum to one.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Random changes in allele frequencies are especially influential in which populations?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Sampling effects can cause strong random changes in small populations.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Movement of alleles between populations through migration and reproduction is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Gene flow transfers genetic variants between populations.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Fossils provide evidence about what?
options: Exact genotype of every living organism
Past life and changes through geological time
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Fossils document organisms and evolutionary changes across geological time.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Structures with a common evolutionary origin but possibly different functions are called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Homologous structures support common ancestry.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Structures that perform similar functions but evolved independently are called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Analogy often results from convergent evolution.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: The formation of new species is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Speciation occurs when populations diverge and become reproductively isolated.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The spread of antibiotic resistance in bacteria is an example of evolution by what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Antibiotics select for resistant variants.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: An organism or agent that can cause disease is called a what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Pathogens include certain bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Malaria is caused by which genus of protozoan parasites?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Plasmodium species cause malaria.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Malaria is transmitted by the bite of an infected female mosquito of which genus?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Dengue is caused by which type of pathogen?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Dengue is caused by dengue viruses.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Tuberculosis is caused by which organism?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which cells differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Activated B cells can differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Vaccination primarily aims to generate what?
options: Immediate replacement of all white cells
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Vaccines stimulate immune responses and memory against specific pathogens.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Cancer is characterised by abnormal, uncontrolled what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Cancer involves uncontrolled cell growth and may invade other tissues.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: HIV primarily attacks which immune cells?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: HIV targets CD4-positive immune cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: An exaggerated immune response to a normally harmless substance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Allergies are hypersensitivity responses to specific allergens.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which microbes help convert milk into curd?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Lactic acid bacteria ferment lactose and acidify milk.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which microorganism is widely used in bread-making and alcoholic fermentation?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Yeast ferments sugars under suitable conditions.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Penicillin was discovered from a mould belonging to which genus?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Penicillium moulds produce penicillin compounds.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which microorganisms produce methane under anaerobic conditions in biogas plants?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Methanogens generate methane in anaerobic digesters.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Activated sludge treatment relies heavily on what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Microorganisms break down organic pollutants in wastewater.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Rhizobium bacteria commonly form nitrogen-fixing associations with which plants?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Rhizobium in legume root nodules fixes atmospheric nitrogen.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Mycorrhiza is an association between plant roots and what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Mycorrhizal fungi can improve uptake of minerals.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Using living organisms to manage pests is known as what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Biological control uses natural enemies or antagonists to reduce pests.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Biochemical oxygen demand is used as an indicator of what in water?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Higher BOD generally indicates greater oxygen demand from biodegradable matter.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Antibiotics are primarily used against susceptible infections caused by what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Antibiotics act against bacteria and do not directly treat viral infections.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific DNA sequences and do what?
options: Cut DNA at or near those sequences
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sites.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which enzyme joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: What is the main purpose of polymerase chain reaction?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: PCR produces many copies of a target DNA segment.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A small circular DNA molecule often used as a cloning vector is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Plasmids can carry inserted DNA into host cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Why are selectable markers used in cloning vectors?
options: To identify or select cells carrying the vector
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Selectable markers help distinguish transformed cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: A bioreactor provides controlled conditions for what?
options: Biological production using cells or enzymes
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Bioreactors control pH, temperature, aeration and other conditions.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: DNA fragments are separated during agarose gel electrophoresis mainly according to what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Smaller DNA fragments usually move farther through agarose gel.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: DNA formed by joining genetic material from different sources is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Recombinant DNA combines sequences from different sources.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which vector feature allows DNA replication to begin in a host cell?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The origin of replication is where replication machinery initiates copying.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: In genetic engineering, competent cells are capable of doing what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Competent cells are prepared to take up DNA.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Bt cotton contains genes derived from which bacterium?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Bt genes can enable plants to produce proteins toxic to certain insect pests.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: RNA interference can silence gene expression through which type of molecule?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: RNA interference uses small RNA molecules to reduce specific RNA transcripts.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Gene therapy aims to treat disease by introducing or modifying what?
options: Genetic material or gene function in cells
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Gene therapy seeks to alter gene function or expression.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Recombinant human insulin can be produced using which general technology?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Recombinant DNA methods enable microbes to produce human insulin.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: An organism carrying introduced genetic material is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Transgenic organisms contain introduced genetic material.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: ELISA commonly detects a target using specific binding between antigen and what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: ELISA uses antigen-antibody recognition and an enzyme-linked signal.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: PCR can help diagnose some infections by detecting what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: PCR amplifies pathogen-specific nucleic acid targets.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Why is biosafety assessment important before releasing a genetically modified organism?
options: To guarantee zero risk without testing
To assess potential risks to health and the environment
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Risk assessment evaluates potential hazards and exposure pathways.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Golden rice was developed to increase which nutrient precursor in rice endosperm?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Golden rice is engineered to accumulate beta-carotene, a provitamin A carotenoid.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A patent related to a biological invention or process is commonly called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Biopatents concern qualifying biological inventions subject to applicable law.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: A population consists of individuals of the same species living in what context?
options: The same area at the same time
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Population ecology studies members of a species sharing an area and time.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: The place where an organism lives is called its what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Habitat refers to the physical place an organism occupies.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: The ecological role and resource use of a species are described by its what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: A niche describes how a species uses resources and interacts with its environment.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The maximum population size an environment can sustain over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Carrying capacity depends on resources and environmental conditions.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Under ideal conditions with unlimited resources, population growth may form which curve?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Exponential growth accelerates when limiting factors are absent.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Population growth that slows as it approaches carrying capacity is represented by which curve?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Logistic growth includes density-dependent limitation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: In mutualism, how are the two species affected?
options: One benefits and the other is always harmed
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Mutualism is an interaction in which both partners benefit.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: In parasitism, which organism benefits while the other is harmed?
options: Host benefits and parasite is harmed
Parasite benefits and host is harmed
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Parasites obtain resources from hosts, often causing harm.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: In commensalism, what is the typical relationship?
options: One species benefits while the other is not significantly affected
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Commensalism benefits one species without a major effect on the other.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: In predation, the predator generally does what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Predators obtain food by capturing or consuming prey.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: An ecosystem includes a community of organisms and what else?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: An ecosystem includes living organisms and their physical environment.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which organisms form the first trophic level in most ecosystems?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Producers capture energy, commonly through photosynthesis.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which organisms break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Fungi and bacteria commonly act as decomposers.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Energy flow through an ecosystem is generally what?
options: Unidirectional, with energy lost as heat at each transfer
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Energy dissipates as heat and is not recycled like nutrients.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Lindeman's ten percent law describes approximately how much energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Only a small fraction, often approximated as 10%, passes to the next trophic level.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which ecological pyramid is always upright?
options: Pyramid of biomass in every case
Pyramid of numbers in every case
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Energy decreases at successive trophic levels.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Primary productivity refers to the rate at which producers do what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Primary productivity is the rate of biomass or organic matter production.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which process is part of decomposition?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Decomposition includes fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralisation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: The gradual change in community composition over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Succession describes changes in ecological communities over time.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Unlike energy, nutrients in ecosystems generally do what?
options: Cycle between organisms and the environment
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Elements such as carbon and nitrogen cycle through biotic and abiotic components.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Biodiversity includes variation at genetic, species and what other level?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Biodiversity is considered at genetic, species and ecosystem levels.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: A species naturally restricted to a particular geographic region is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Endemic species have naturally limited geographic distributions.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Protecting species in their natural habitats is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: In situ conservation protects organisms within their natural ecosystems.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is an example of ex situ conservation?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Seed banks preserve plant genetic material outside its natural habitat.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which organisation publishes the widely used Red List of Threatened Species?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The International Union for Conservation of Nature maintains the Red List.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: A biodiversity hotspot is identified by high endemism and what other feature?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Hotspots combine high endemism with substantial habitat loss.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: A species with a disproportionately large ecological effect relative to its abundance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Keystone species strongly influence ecosystem structure and function.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Breaking a continuous habitat into smaller, isolated patches is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Fragmentation can isolate populations and increase edge effects.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: A species is extinct when what condition is met?
options: It moves to another local habitat
Its population decreases for one season
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Extinction means the species no longer has living individuals.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which action supports long-term biodiversity conservation?
options: Protecting habitats and reducing major threats
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Habitat protection and threat reduction are central conservation measures.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which gas is a major contributor to human-driven global warming?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels and land-use change contribute to warming.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which chemicals historically contributed significantly to stratospheric ozone depletion?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: CFC-derived chlorine radicals can catalyse ozone destruction.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Excess nutrient enrichment of a water body that can cause algal blooms is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus can promote algal growth and oxygen depletion.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: An increase in concentration of persistent pollutants at higher trophic levels is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Persistent pollutants can accumulate through food chains.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Acid rain is mainly associated with atmospheric emissions of which gases?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Sulfur and nitrogen oxides form acids in the atmosphere.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which practice can reduce the amount of waste sent to landfills?
options: Mixing hazardous waste with food waste
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Waste prevention and recovery reduce landfill pressure.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Sound levels are commonly expressed in which unit?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Sound pressure levels are commonly expressed in decibels.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which is a renewable energy source?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Solar energy is replenished naturally on human timescales.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: The build-up of a substance in an organism over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Bioaccumulation occurs when uptake exceeds elimination.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Establishing forest cover on land not recently forested is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Afforestation establishes tree cover on suitable land.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which type of reproduction usually involves one parent and no fusion of gametes?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Asexual reproduction generally involves one parent and does not involve gamete fusion.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Amoeba commonly reproduces asexually by which method?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: In binary fission, one parent cell divides into two daughter cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which organism commonly reproduces asexually by budding?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Hydra can form a new individual as an outgrowth or bud.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Growing a new plant from a stem cutting is an example of what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Vegetative propagation uses vegetative plant parts to produce new plants.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: The fusion of male and female gametes is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Fertilisation combines the nuclei of compatible gametes.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Development of an individual from an unfertilised egg is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Parthenogenesis is development without fertilisation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Asexual reproductive units produced by many fungi are called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Spores can germinate and develop into new individuals under suitable conditions.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A group of genetically identical individuals produced asexually is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Asexual reproduction often produces genetically similar or identical offspring.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: In which type of fertilisation do gametes unite outside the body?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: External fertilisation occurs outside the parental body, often in water.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: The period from birth to natural death of an organism is called its what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Life span is the duration between birth and natural death.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which part of a typical angiosperm stamen produces pollen grains?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The anther contains microsporangia where pollen grains develop.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The formation of microspores from pollen mother cells by meiosis is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Microsporogenesis produces haploid microspores by meiosis.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which highly resistant material is found in the exine of pollen grains?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Sporopollenin is highly resistant to chemical and biological degradation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: A typical mature angiosperm embryo sac usually has how many cells and nuclei?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The common Polygonum-type embryo sac has seven cells and eight nuclei.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Pollination places pollen on a receptive stigma.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Double fertilisation in angiosperms consists of which two events?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: One male gamete fuses with the egg; the other fuses with the polar nuclei/secondary nucleus.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: In a typical angiosperm, the primary endosperm nucleus is usually what ploidy?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Triple fusion commonly produces a triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Seed formation without fertilisation is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Apomixis can produce seeds without normal fertilisation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Development of a fruit without fertilisation is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Parthenocarpy results in fruit development without fertilisation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is an example of an outbreeding device in flowering plants?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Dichogamy separates pollen release and stigma receptivity in time.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: The production of sperm cells is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Spermatogenesis occurs in the seminiferous tubules of the testes.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which testicular cells secrete testosterone?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Leydig cells secrete androgens.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which cells support and nourish developing sperm cells in seminiferous tubules?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Sertoli cells support developing germ cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The formation of female gametes is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Oogenesis is the process of forming ova.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: The release of a secondary oocyte from a mature ovarian follicle is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Ovulation releases a secondary oocyte from the ovary.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which structure forms from the ruptured follicle after ovulation?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The corpus luteum secretes progesterone.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Where does fertilisation normally occur in humans?
options: Ampullary-isthmic region of the uterine tube
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Human fertilisation normally occurs at the ampullary-isthmic junction of the oviduct.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The attachment of the blastocyst to the uterine endometrium is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Implantation embeds the blastocyst in the uterine lining.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which temporary organ facilitates exchange between maternal and foetal blood systems?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The placenta supports exchange and also functions as an endocrine tissue.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which hormone primarily stimulates milk production after childbirth?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Prolactin stimulates milk synthesis; oxytocin helps milk ejection.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: What is the main purpose of contraceptive methods?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Contraception helps prevent unintended pregnancy.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which barrier method can also reduce transmission risk of many sexually transmitted infections?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Correct condom use reduces pregnancy and STI transmission risk.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Copper-releasing intrauterine devices are primarily used to prevent what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Copper IUDs interfere with sperm function and reduce the chance of fertilisation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: In which assisted reproductive technique is fertilisation initiated outside the body?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: IVF involves fertilising an oocyte outside the body before embryo transfer.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which surgical procedure is a method of male sterilisation?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Vasectomy blocks or cuts the vas deferens.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which surgical procedure is a method of female sterilisation?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Tubectomy blocks or cuts the fallopian tubes.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which action helps reduce the risk of sexually transmitted infections?
options: Correct condom use and appropriate testing
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Prevention includes barrier protection, testing and timely medical care.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Amniocentesis involves sampling which fluid for certain prenatal tests?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Amniotic fluid may contain foetal cells useful for selected diagnostic tests.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: What is the most appropriate next step when a couple has concerns about infertility?
options: Seek assessment from a qualified healthcare professional
Assume one partner is always responsible
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Infertility may have multiple causes and should be evaluated appropriately.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which technique involves placing processed semen into the female reproductive tract?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Artificial insemination introduces semen into the reproductive tract by a medical procedure.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: A gene is best described as what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Genes are DNA sequences that contribute to functional products and inherited traits.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Alternative forms of the same gene are called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Alleles occupy corresponding loci and can contribute to variation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: The genetic constitution of an organism for a trait is its what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Genotype refers to genetic makeup.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The observable characteristics of an organism are called its what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Phenotype reflects genotype and environmental influences.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which ABO blood group phenotype expresses both A and B antigens on red blood cells?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The AB phenotype expresses both A and B antigens.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: In the human ABO blood group system, IA and IB alleles show what relationship?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Both IA and IB are expressed in the AB phenotype.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: A gene with more than two alternative forms in a population is said to have what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: A population may contain multiple alleles, though a diploid individual carries at most two.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The Rh-positive phenotype commonly reflects the presence of which red-cell antigen?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The D antigen is the major antigen used in routine Rh classification.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: A heritable change in DNA sequence is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Mutations can create new genetic variants.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which chart is used to trace inheritance of a trait through family generations?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Pedigree charts help analyse inheritance patterns in families.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which molecule is the principal hereditary material in most organisms?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: DNA stores hereditary information in most organisms.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which components make up a nucleotide?
options: Sugar, phosphate group and nitrogenous base
Amino acid and fatty acid only
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: A nucleotide consists of a pentose sugar, phosphate group and nitrogenous base.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which base pairs with adenine in DNA?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which nitrogenous base occurs in RNA in place of thymine?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: RNA typically contains uracil instead of thymine.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Why is DNA replication described as semiconservative?
options: Each daughter molecule contains one parental and one newly synthesised strand
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Each daughter double helix retains one original strand.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The synthesis of RNA using DNA as a template is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Transcription produces RNA from a DNA template.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: The process by which ribosomes use mRNA to synthesise a polypeptide is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Translation converts mRNA codon information into an amino-acid sequence.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: A sequence of three nucleotides in mRNA that specifies an amino acid or stop signal is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Codons are read in triplets during translation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which RNA molecule carries amino acids to the ribosome?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: tRNA carries amino acids and pairs its anticodon with an mRNA codon.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: DNA fingerprinting commonly compares which type of variation?
options: Variable DNA regions such as STRs
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Variable DNA markers can help distinguish individuals.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Natural selection acts on heritable variation that affects what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Individuals with advantageous heritable traits may leave more offspring.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: A heritable feature that improves reproductive success in a particular environment is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Adaptations can increase fitness in a given environment.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, what is the relationship between allele frequencies p and q for a two-allele locus?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: For two alleles, their frequencies sum to one.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Random changes in allele frequencies are especially influential in which populations?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Sampling effects can cause strong random changes in small populations.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Movement of alleles between populations through migration and reproduction is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Gene flow transfers genetic variants between populations.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Fossils provide evidence about what?
options: Exact genotype of every living organism
Past life and changes through geological time
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Fossils document organisms and evolutionary changes across geological time.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Structures with a common evolutionary origin but possibly different functions are called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Homologous structures support common ancestry.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Structures that perform similar functions but evolved independently are called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Analogy often results from convergent evolution.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: The formation of new species is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Speciation occurs when populations diverge and become reproductively isolated.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: The spread of antibiotic resistance in bacteria is an example of evolution by what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Antibiotics select for resistant variants.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: An organism or agent that can cause disease is called a what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Pathogens include certain bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Malaria is caused by which genus of protozoan parasites?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Plasmodium species cause malaria.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Malaria is transmitted by the bite of an infected female mosquito of which genus?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Dengue is caused by which type of pathogen?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Dengue is caused by dengue viruses.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Tuberculosis is caused by which organism?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which cells differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Activated B cells can differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Vaccination primarily aims to generate what?
options: Immediate replacement of all white cells
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Vaccines stimulate immune responses and memory against specific pathogens.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Cancer is characterised by abnormal, uncontrolled what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Cancer involves uncontrolled cell growth and may invade other tissues.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: HIV primarily attacks which immune cells?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: HIV targets CD4-positive immune cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: An exaggerated immune response to a normally harmless substance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Allergies are hypersensitivity responses to specific allergens.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which microbes help convert milk into curd?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Lactic acid bacteria ferment lactose and acidify milk.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which microorganism is widely used in bread-making and alcoholic fermentation?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Yeast ferments sugars under suitable conditions.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Penicillin was discovered from a mould belonging to which genus?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Penicillium moulds produce penicillin compounds.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which microorganisms produce methane under anaerobic conditions in biogas plants?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Methanogens generate methane in anaerobic digesters.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Activated sludge treatment relies heavily on what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Microorganisms break down organic pollutants in wastewater.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Rhizobium bacteria commonly form nitrogen-fixing associations with which plants?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Rhizobium in legume root nodules fixes atmospheric nitrogen.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Mycorrhiza is an association between plant roots and what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Mycorrhizal fungi can improve uptake of minerals.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Using living organisms to manage pests is known as what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Biological control uses natural enemies or antagonists to reduce pests.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Biochemical oxygen demand is used as an indicator of what in water?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Higher BOD generally indicates greater oxygen demand from biodegradable matter.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Antibiotics are primarily used against susceptible infections caused by what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Antibiotics act against bacteria and do not directly treat viral infections.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific DNA sequences and do what?
options: Cut DNA at or near those sequences
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sites.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which enzyme joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: What is the main purpose of polymerase chain reaction?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: PCR produces many copies of a target DNA segment.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: A small circular DNA molecule often used as a cloning vector is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Plasmids can carry inserted DNA into host cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Why are selectable markers used in cloning vectors?
options: To identify or select cells carrying the vector
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Selectable markers help distinguish transformed cells.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A bioreactor provides controlled conditions for what?
options: Biological production using cells or enzymes
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Bioreactors control pH, temperature, aeration and other conditions.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: DNA fragments are separated during agarose gel electrophoresis mainly according to what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Smaller DNA fragments usually move farther through agarose gel.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: DNA formed by joining genetic material from different sources is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Recombinant DNA combines sequences from different sources.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which vector feature allows DNA replication to begin in a host cell?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The origin of replication is where replication machinery initiates copying.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: In genetic engineering, competent cells are capable of doing what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Competent cells are prepared to take up DNA.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Bt cotton contains genes derived from which bacterium?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Bt genes can enable plants to produce proteins toxic to certain insect pests.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: RNA interference can silence gene expression through which type of molecule?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: RNA interference uses small RNA molecules to reduce specific RNA transcripts.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Gene therapy aims to treat disease by introducing or modifying what?
options: Genetic material or gene function in cells
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Gene therapy seeks to alter gene function or expression.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Recombinant human insulin can be produced using which general technology?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Recombinant DNA methods enable microbes to produce human insulin.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: An organism carrying introduced genetic material is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Transgenic organisms contain introduced genetic material.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: ELISA commonly detects a target using specific binding between antigen and what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: ELISA uses antigen-antibody recognition and an enzyme-linked signal.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: PCR can help diagnose some infections by detecting what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: PCR amplifies pathogen-specific nucleic acid targets.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Why is biosafety assessment important before releasing a genetically modified organism?
options: To assess potential risks to health and the environment
To guarantee zero risk without testing
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Risk assessment evaluates potential hazards and exposure pathways.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Golden rice was developed to increase which nutrient precursor in rice endosperm?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Golden rice is engineered to accumulate beta-carotene, a provitamin A carotenoid.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: A patent related to a biological invention or process is commonly called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Biopatents concern qualifying biological inventions subject to applicable law.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: A population consists of individuals of the same species living in what context?
options: The same area at the same time
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Population ecology studies members of a species sharing an area and time.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The place where an organism lives is called its what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Habitat refers to the physical place an organism occupies.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: The ecological role and resource use of a species are described by its what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: A niche describes how a species uses resources and interacts with its environment.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: The maximum population size an environment can sustain over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Carrying capacity depends on resources and environmental conditions.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Under ideal conditions with unlimited resources, population growth may form which curve?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Exponential growth accelerates when limiting factors are absent.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Population growth that slows as it approaches carrying capacity is represented by which curve?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Logistic growth includes density-dependent limitation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: In mutualism, how are the two species affected?
options: One benefits and the other is always harmed
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Mutualism is an interaction in which both partners benefit.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: In parasitism, which organism benefits while the other is harmed?
options: Host benefits and parasite is harmed
Parasite benefits and host is harmed
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Parasites obtain resources from hosts, often causing harm.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: In commensalism, what is the typical relationship?
options: One species benefits while the other is not significantly affected
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Commensalism benefits one species without a major effect on the other.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: In predation, the predator generally does what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Predators obtain food by capturing or consuming prey.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: An ecosystem includes a community of organisms and what else?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: An ecosystem includes living organisms and their physical environment.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which organisms form the first trophic level in most ecosystems?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Producers capture energy, commonly through photosynthesis.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which organisms break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Fungi and bacteria commonly act as decomposers.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Energy flow through an ecosystem is generally what?
options: Unidirectional, with energy lost as heat at each transfer
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Energy dissipates as heat and is not recycled like nutrients.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Lindeman's ten percent law describes approximately how much energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Only a small fraction, often approximated as 10%, passes to the next trophic level.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which ecological pyramid is always upright?
options: Pyramid of biomass in every case
Pyramid of numbers in every case
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Energy decreases at successive trophic levels.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Primary productivity refers to the rate at which producers do what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Primary productivity is the rate of biomass or organic matter production.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which process is part of decomposition?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Decomposition includes fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralisation.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: The gradual change in community composition over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Succession describes changes in ecological communities over time.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Unlike energy, nutrients in ecosystems generally do what?
options: Cycle between organisms and the environment
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Elements such as carbon and nitrogen cycle through biotic and abiotic components.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Biodiversity includes variation at genetic, species and what other level?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Biodiversity is considered at genetic, species and ecosystem levels.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A species naturally restricted to a particular geographic region is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Endemic species have naturally limited geographic distributions.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Protecting species in their natural habitats is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: In situ conservation protects organisms within their natural ecosystems.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which is an example of ex situ conservation?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Seed banks preserve plant genetic material outside its natural habitat.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Which organisation publishes the widely used Red List of Threatened Species?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: The International Union for Conservation of Nature maintains the Red List.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A biodiversity hotspot is identified by high endemism and what other feature?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Hotspots combine high endemism with substantial habitat loss.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: A species with a disproportionately large ecological effect relative to its abundance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Keystone species strongly influence ecosystem structure and function.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Breaking a continuous habitat into smaller, isolated patches is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Fragmentation can isolate populations and increase edge effects.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: A species is extinct when what condition is met?
options: It moves to another local habitat
Its population decreases for one season
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Extinction means the species no longer has living individuals.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which action supports long-term biodiversity conservation?
options: Protecting habitats and reducing major threats
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Habitat protection and threat reduction are central conservation measures.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Which gas is a major contributor to human-driven global warming?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels and land-use change contribute to warming.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which chemicals historically contributed significantly to stratospheric ozone depletion?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: CFC-derived chlorine radicals can catalyse ozone destruction.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Excess nutrient enrichment of a water body that can cause algal blooms is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus can promote algal growth and oxygen depletion.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: An increase in concentration of persistent pollutants at higher trophic levels is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Persistent pollutants can accumulate through food chains.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: Acid rain is mainly associated with atmospheric emissions of which gases?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Sulfur and nitrogen oxides form acids in the atmosphere.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Which practice can reduce the amount of waste sent to landfills?
options: Mixing hazardous waste with food waste
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Waste prevention and recovery reduce landfill pressure.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Revision check: Sound levels are commonly expressed in which unit?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Sound pressure levels are commonly expressed in decibels.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is a renewable energy source?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Solar energy is replenished naturally on human timescales.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Choose the best answer: The build-up of a substance in an organism over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Bioaccumulation occurs when uptake exceeds elimination.

CBSE 12 - Biology.q: Quick review: Establishing forest cover on land not recently forested is called what?
CBSE 12 - Biology.why: Afforestation establishes tree cover on suitable land.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Biotechnology uses living organisms or biological systems to develop products and processes. Which technique is commonly used to amplify DNA?
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplifies selected DNA sequences.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which enzyme joins DNA fragments together?
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Restriction endonucleases recognise:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Restriction endonucleases cut DNA at particular recognition sequences.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: A plasmid is commonly used in genetic engineering as a:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Plasmids can act as vectors to carry foreign DNA into host cells.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: The enzyme used to synthesise DNA from an RNA template is:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Reverse transcriptase synthesises complementary DNA using RNA as a template.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: PCR commonly uses which thermostable DNA polymerase?
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Taq polymerase remains active through PCR's high-temperature cycles.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: In gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments are separated mainly according to:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: DNA fragments migrate through the gel at rates related to their size; smaller fragments usually travel farther.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: A selectable marker helps researchers to:
options: Identify cells carrying a desired vector
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Selectable markers help distinguish cells that have taken up a vector.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: The process of introducing recombinant DNA into a host cell is often called:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Transformation is a common term for introducing foreign DNA into a host cell.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: A bioreactor is designed to:
options: Provide controlled conditions for biological production
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Bioreactors maintain controlled conditions for large-scale biological processes.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Recombinant human insulin is produced using:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Recombinant DNA technology enables microorganisms to produce human insulin.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Bt cotton has been engineered for resistance to certain:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Bt cotton expresses insecticidal proteins derived from Bacillus thuringiensis that target certain insect pests.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: The organism from which Bt insecticidal genes were obtained is:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Bt refers to Bacillus thuringiensis.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Gene therapy aims to:
options: Treat a disorder by introducing or modifying genetic material
Prevent all inherited conditions with certainty
Change every trait in every patient
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Gene therapy seeks to treat disease by adding, replacing or modifying genetic material in target cells.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: ELISA is commonly used to detect:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: ELISA uses antigen-antibody interactions to detect specific targets.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: A transgenic organism contains:
options: Genetic material introduced using genetic engineering
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: A transgenic organism carries introduced genetic material, often from another source.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: RNA interference can be used to:
options: Silence expression of a target gene
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: RNA interference can reduce expression of a target gene by targeting its RNA.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Molecular diagnosis can help identify diseases by detecting:
options: Specific DNA, RNA, proteins or immune markers
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Molecular diagnostics detect disease-associated molecular markers.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which of the following is a biological product made using recombinant technology?
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Recombinant human insulin is a well-known biotechnology product.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: A major ethical concern in biotechnology is:
options: Privacy and responsible use of genetic information
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Genetic privacy, consent, safety and equitable access are important ethical concerns.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: DNA is made up of repeating units called:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: DNA is a polymer of nucleotides.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: In DNA, adenine pairs with:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: In standard DNA base pairing, adenine pairs with thymine.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: The process of making RNA from a DNA template is:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Transcription synthesises RNA from a DNA template.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: The process of synthesising a protein using mRNA is:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Translation uses the codons in mRNA to assemble a polypeptide.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: A codon consists of how many nucleotides?
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: A codon is a sequence of three nucleotides.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: An organism's observable characteristics are called its:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Phenotype refers to observable traits produced by genotype and environment.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: An allele is:
options: An alternative form of a gene
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Alleles are alternative forms of the same gene.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: The enzyme that unwinds the DNA double helix during replication is:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Helicase separates DNA strands during replication.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: A mutation is:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: A mutation is a change in DNA sequence or other genetic material.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: A gene is generally a segment of nucleic acid that contributes to:
options: A functional product or its regulation
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Genes encode functional RNAs or products such as proteins and can regulate biological functions.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: The basic structural and functional unit of life is the:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: The cell is the basic unit of life.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which organelle is the major site of aerobic respiration in eukaryotic cells?
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Mitochondria generate much of the ATP during aerobic respiration.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Ribosomes are primarily responsible for:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Ribosomes translate mRNA to synthesise proteins.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Bacteria are generally classified as:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Bacteria are prokaryotic organisms that lack a membrane-bound nucleus.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Aseptic technique is used to:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Aseptic technique helps prevent contamination of samples and cultures.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: An autoclave sterilises materials using:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Autoclaves use pressurised steam at high temperature to sterilise suitable materials.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: A culture medium provides microorganisms with:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Culture media supply nutrients needed for microbial growth.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Viruses reproduce by:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Viruses depend on host cells to replicate.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Fermentation is widely used in biotechnology to:
options: Make every product sterile without processing
Produce useful products using cells or microorganisms
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Fermentation uses microorganisms or cells to produce useful compounds under controlled conditions.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Downstream processing refers to:
options: Recovery and purification of a product after production
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Downstream processing includes separation, recovery and purification of the product.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: A fermenter typically controls variables such as:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Bioreactors control process variables such as temperature, pH, aeration and agitation.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: An enzyme used in an industrial process is valued for its ability to:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Enzymes act as biological catalysts and can provide reaction specificity.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: A monoclonal antibody is designed to bind:
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Monoclonal antibodies recognise a particular antigen or epitope.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: A vaccine aims to:
options: Cause the same disease in every person
Train the immune system to respond to a target pathogen or antigen
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Vaccines stimulate immune memory and help protect against targeted infections.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: A biosensor combines a biological recognition element with:
options: A system that produces a measurable signal
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Biosensors convert a biological interaction into a measurable signal.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Bioremediation uses organisms to:
options: Help remove or break down pollutants
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Bioremediation uses biological activity to reduce or remove environmental contaminants.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Which enzyme joins DNA fragments together? (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Restriction endonucleases recognise: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Restriction endonucleases cut DNA at particular recognition sequences.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? A plasmid is commonly used in genetic engineering as a: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Plasmids can act as vectors to carry foreign DNA into host cells.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? The enzyme used to synthesise DNA from an RNA template is: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Reverse transcriptase synthesises complementary DNA using RNA as a template.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? PCR commonly uses which thermostable DNA polymerase? (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Taq polymerase remains active through PCR's high-temperature cycles.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? In gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments are separated mainly according to: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: DNA fragments migrate through the gel at rates related to their size; smaller fragments usually travel farther.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? A selectable marker helps researchers to: (CBSE practice question)
options: Identify cells carrying a desired vector
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Selectable markers help distinguish cells that have taken up a vector.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? The process of introducing recombinant DNA into a host cell is often called: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Transformation is a common term for introducing foreign DNA into a host cell.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? A bioreactor is designed to: (CBSE practice question)
options: Provide controlled conditions for biological production
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Bioreactors maintain controlled conditions for large-scale biological processes.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Recombinant human insulin is produced using: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Recombinant DNA technology enables microorganisms to produce human insulin.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Bt cotton has been engineered for resistance to certain: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Bt cotton expresses insecticidal proteins derived from Bacillus thuringiensis that target certain insect pests.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? The organism from which Bt insecticidal genes were obtained is: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Bt refers to Bacillus thuringiensis.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Gene therapy aims to: (CBSE practice question)
options: Treat a disorder by introducing or modifying genetic material
Change every trait in every patient
Prevent all inherited conditions with certainty
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Gene therapy seeks to treat disease by adding, replacing or modifying genetic material in target cells.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? ELISA is commonly used to detect: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: ELISA uses antigen-antibody interactions to detect specific targets.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? A transgenic organism contains: (CBSE practice question)
options: Genetic material introduced using genetic engineering
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: A transgenic organism carries introduced genetic material, often from another source.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? RNA interference can be used to: (CBSE practice question)
options: Silence expression of a target gene
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: RNA interference can reduce expression of a target gene by targeting its RNA.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Molecular diagnosis can help identify diseases by detecting: (CBSE practice question)
options: Specific DNA, RNA, proteins or immune markers
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Molecular diagnostics detect disease-associated molecular markers.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Which of the following is a biological product made using recombinant technology? (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Recombinant human insulin is a well-known biotechnology product.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? A major ethical concern in biotechnology is: (CBSE practice question)
options: Privacy and responsible use of genetic information
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Genetic privacy, consent, safety and equitable access are important ethical concerns.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? DNA is made up of repeating units called: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: DNA is a polymer of nucleotides.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? In DNA, adenine pairs with: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: In standard DNA base pairing, adenine pairs with thymine.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? The process of making RNA from a DNA template is: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Transcription synthesises RNA from a DNA template.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? The process of synthesising a protein using mRNA is: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Translation uses the codons in mRNA to assemble a polypeptide.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? A codon consists of how many nucleotides? (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: A codon is a sequence of three nucleotides.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? An organism's observable characteristics are called its: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Phenotype refers to observable traits produced by genotype and environment.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? An allele is: (CBSE practice question)
options: An alternative form of a gene
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Alleles are alternative forms of the same gene.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? The enzyme that unwinds the DNA double helix during replication is: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Helicase separates DNA strands during replication.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? A mutation is: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: A mutation is a change in DNA sequence or other genetic material.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? A gene is generally a segment of nucleic acid that contributes to: (CBSE practice question)
options: A functional product or its regulation
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Genes encode functional RNAs or products such as proteins and can regulate biological functions.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? The basic structural and functional unit of life is the: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: The cell is the basic unit of life.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Which organelle is the major site of aerobic respiration in eukaryotic cells? (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Mitochondria generate much of the ATP during aerobic respiration.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Ribosomes are primarily responsible for: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Ribosomes translate mRNA to synthesise proteins.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Bacteria are generally classified as: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Bacteria are prokaryotic organisms that lack a membrane-bound nucleus.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Aseptic technique is used to: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Aseptic technique helps prevent contamination of samples and cultures.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? An autoclave sterilises materials using: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Autoclaves use pressurised steam at high temperature to sterilise suitable materials.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? A culture medium provides microorganisms with: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Culture media supply nutrients needed for microbial growth.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Viruses reproduce by: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Viruses depend on host cells to replicate.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Fermentation is widely used in biotechnology to: (CBSE practice question)
options: Produce useful products using cells or microorganisms
Make every product sterile without processing
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Fermentation uses microorganisms or cells to produce useful compounds under controlled conditions.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Downstream processing refers to: (CBSE practice question)
options: Recovery and purification of a product after production
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Downstream processing includes separation, recovery and purification of the product.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? A fermenter typically controls variables such as: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Bioreactors control process variables such as temperature, pH, aeration and agitation.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? An enzyme used in an industrial process is valued for its ability to: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Enzymes act as biological catalysts and can provide reaction specificity.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? A monoclonal antibody is designed to bind: (CBSE practice question)
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Monoclonal antibodies recognise a particular antigen or epitope.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? A vaccine aims to: (CBSE practice question)
options: Cause the same disease in every person
Train the immune system to respond to a target pathogen or antigen
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Vaccines stimulate immune memory and help protect against targeted infections.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? A biosensor combines a biological recognition element with: (CBSE practice question)
options: A system that produces a measurable signal
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Biosensors convert a biological interaction into a measurable signal.

CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.q: Which option correctly answers the following? Bioremediation uses organisms to: (CBSE practice question)
options: Help remove or break down pollutants
CBSE 12 - Biotechnology.why: Bioremediation uses biological activity to reduce or remove environmental contaminants.
