CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which part of a typical angiosperm stamen produces pollen grains?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The anther contains microsporangia where pollen grains develop.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: The formation of microspores from pollen mother cells by meiosis is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Microsporogenesis produces haploid microspores by meiosis.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: The outer wall of a pollen grain, called the exine, contains which highly resistant material?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Sporopollenin is highly resistant to chemical and biological degradation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: The typical mature angiosperm embryo sac is usually described as having how many cells and nuclei?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The common Polygonum-type embryo sac has seven cells and eight nuclei.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Pollination places pollen on a receptive stigma.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Double fertilisation in angiosperms consists of which two events?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: One male gamete fuses with the egg; the other fuses with the polar nuclei/secondary nucleus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: In a typical angiosperm, the primary endosperm nucleus is usually what ploidy?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Triple fusion commonly produces a triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Seed formation without fertilisation is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Apomixis can produce seeds without the normal fertilisation process.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Development of a fruit without fertilisation is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Parthenocarpy results in fruit development without fertilisation, often producing seedless fruits.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which is an example of an outbreeding device in flowering plants?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Dichogamy separates pollen release and stigma receptivity in time.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Who is known as the father of genetics?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mendel's pea-plant experiments established foundational principles of inheritance.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Alternative forms of a gene are called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Alleles are alternative versions of a gene at a locus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: A cross that studies the inheritance of one pair of contrasting traits is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: A monohybrid cross follows one trait.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Mendel's law of segregation states that paired alleles separate during what process?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Alleles segregate during gamete formation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: In snapdragon, a red-flowered plant crossed with a white-flowered plant can produce pink offspring. This illustrates what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which human blood group phenotype illustrates codominance of IA and IB alleles?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Both A and B antigens are expressed in the AB phenotype.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: An individual with a dominant phenotype is crossed with a homozygous recessive individual to determine its genotype. This is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: A test cross helps distinguish homozygous dominant from heterozygous genotypes.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Haemophilia is commonly inherited as which type of trait?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Haemophilia A and B are commonly X-linked recessive disorders.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: A sudden heritable change in genetic material is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mutations create new genetic variation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which chart is used to trace the inheritance of a trait through generations?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Pedigree analysis helps infer inheritance patterns in families.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which molecule stores hereditary information in most organisms?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: DNA is the hereditary material in most organisms.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: A nucleotide consists of which components?
options: A pentose sugar, phosphate group and nitrogenous base
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Nucleotides are the building blocks of nucleic acids.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which base pairs with adenine in DNA?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Why is DNA replication described as semiconservative?
options: Each daughter DNA molecule contains one parental and one new strand
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Each daughter double helix retains one original strand.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Synthesis of RNA using DNA as a template is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Transcription copies information from DNA into RNA.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which cellular structure reads mRNA to synthesise a polypeptide?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Ribosomes translate mRNA codons into an amino-acid sequence.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: A three-nucleotide sequence on mRNA is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Codons specify amino acids or translation termination.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which RNA carries amino acids to the ribosome during translation?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: tRNA delivers amino acids and pairs its anticodon with mRNA codons.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: In the lac operon, lactose or its derivative acts as what when present?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The inducer inactivates the repressor and permits transcription of structural genes.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which was a major aim of the Human Genome Project?
options: Sequencing and mapping the human genome
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The project aimed to identify and map human genes and determine DNA sequence.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Natural selection favours heritable traits that improve what in a particular environment?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Traits that improve survival and reproduction can become more common.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Fossils provide evidence about what?
options: The exact DNA of every living species
Past life and evolutionary change through geological time
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Fossils document organisms from earlier geological periods.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Organs with a common evolutionary origin but different functions are called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Homology supports common ancestry.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Wings of birds and insects are often cited as examples of what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: They perform similar functions but evolved independently.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Random changes in allele frequencies are generally strongest in which populations?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Random sampling has a larger effect in small populations.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Movement of alleles between populations due to migration and reproduction is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Gene flow transfers alleles among populations.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: For a gene with two alleles at frequencies p and q, what is the relationship under the Hardy-Weinberg model?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Allele frequencies sum to one for a two-allele locus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: The formation of new species is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Speciation involves divergence and reproductive isolation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Evolution of multiple species from a common ancestor into different ecological niches is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Adaptive radiation is diversification from a common ancestor into different niches.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: The spread of antibiotic resistance in bacteria is an example of evolution by what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Antibiotics select for resistant variants already present or arising by mutation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: An agent that causes disease is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Pathogens include certain bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Malaria is caused by which type of organism?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Plasmodium species are protozoan parasites that cause malaria.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Malaria is transmitted by the bite of an infected female mosquito of which genus?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium parasites.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Dengue is caused by which type of pathogen?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Dengue is caused by dengue viruses.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Tuberculosis is caused by which organism?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which cells differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Activated B cells can differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Vaccination primarily aims to generate what?
options: Immediate replacement of all white cells
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Vaccines stimulate immune responses and memory against specific pathogens.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Cancer is characterised by abnormal, uncontrolled what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Cancer involves uncontrolled cell growth and may invade other tissues.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: HIV primarily attacks which immune cells?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: HIV targets CD4-positive immune cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: An exaggerated immune response to a normally harmless substance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Allergy is a hypersensitivity response to an allergen.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which microbes help convert milk into curd?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Lactic acid bacteria ferment lactose and acidify milk.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which microorganism is used in bread-making and alcoholic fermentation?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Yeast ferments sugars and releases carbon dioxide and ethanol under suitable conditions.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Penicillin was discovered from a mould belonging to which genus?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Penicillium moulds produce penicillin compounds.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which microorganisms produce methane under anaerobic conditions in biogas plants?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Methanogens generate methane in anaerobic digesters.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Activated sludge treatment relies heavily on what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Microorganisms break down organic pollutants in wastewater.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Rhizobium bacteria commonly form nitrogen-fixing associations with which plants?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Rhizobium in legume root nodules fixes atmospheric nitrogen.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Mycorrhiza is an association between plant roots and what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mycorrhizal fungi can improve uptake of minerals such as phosphorus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Using living organisms to control pests is known as what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Biological control uses natural enemies or antagonists to reduce pests.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Biochemical oxygen demand is used as an indicator of what in water?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Higher BOD generally indicates greater oxygen demand from biodegradable matter.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Antibiotics are substances used to inhibit or kill susceptible what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Antibiotics act against bacteria and do not directly treat viral infections.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific DNA sequences and do what?
options: Cut DNA at or near those sequences
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sites.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which enzyme joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: What is the primary purpose of polymerase chain reaction?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: PCR produces many copies of a target DNA segment.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: A small circular DNA molecule often used as a cloning vector is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Plasmids can carry inserted DNA into host cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Why are selectable markers used in cloning vectors?
options: To identify or select cells carrying the vector
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Selectable markers help distinguish transformed cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: A bioreactor provides controlled conditions for what?
options: Biological production using cells or enzymes
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Bioreactors control factors such as pH, temperature and aeration.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: DNA fragments are separated during agarose gel electrophoresis mainly according to what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: DNA fragments migrate through the gel; smaller fragments usually move farther.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: DNA formed by joining genetic material from different sources is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Recombinant DNA combines DNA sequences from different sources.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which vector feature allows DNA replication to begin in a host cell?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The origin of replication is the site where replication machinery initiates copying.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: In genetic engineering, competent cells are cells capable of doing what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Competent cells are prepared to take up DNA.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Bt cotton contains genes derived from which bacterium?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Bt genes can enable plants to produce proteins toxic to certain insect pests.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: RNA interference can silence gene expression through which type of molecule?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: RNAi uses small RNA molecules to target and reduce specific RNA transcripts.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Gene therapy aims to treat disease by introducing or modifying what?
options: Genetic material or gene function in cells
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Gene therapy seeks to alter gene function or expression.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Recombinant human insulin is produced using which general technology?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Recombinant DNA methods can enable microbes to produce human insulin.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: An organism carrying introduced genetic material is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Transgenic organisms contain genetic material introduced through genetic engineering.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: ELISA commonly detects a target using specific binding between antigen and what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: ELISA uses antigen-antibody recognition and an enzyme-linked signal.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: PCR can help diagnose some infections by detecting what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: PCR can amplify pathogen-specific DNA or, with reverse transcription, RNA-derived targets.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Why is biosafety assessment important when releasing a genetically modified organism?
options: To assess potential risks to health and the environment
To guarantee zero risk without testing
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Risk assessment evaluates potential hazards and exposure pathways.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Golden rice was developed to increase the level of which nutrient precursor in rice endosperm?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Golden rice is engineered to accumulate beta-carotene, a provitamin A carotenoid.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: A patent related to a biological invention or process is commonly called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Biopatents concern qualifying biological inventions, subject to applicable law.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: A population consists of individuals of the same species living in what context?
options: The same area at the same time
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Population ecology studies members of a species sharing an area and time.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: The place where an organism lives is called its what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Habitat refers to the physical place an organism occupies.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: The ecological role and resource use of a species are described by its what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: A niche describes how a species uses resources and interacts with its environment.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: The maximum population size an environment can sustain over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Carrying capacity depends on resources and environmental conditions.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Under ideal conditions with unlimited resources, population growth may form which curve?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Exponential growth accelerates when limiting factors are absent.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Population growth that slows as it approaches carrying capacity is represented by which curve?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Logistic growth includes density-dependent limitation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: In mutualism, how are the two species affected?
options: One benefits and the other is always harmed
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mutualism is an interaction in which both partners benefit.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: In parasitism, which organism benefits while the other is harmed?
options: Host benefits and parasite is harmed
Parasite benefits and host is harmed
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Parasites obtain resources from hosts, often causing harm.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: In commensalism, what is the typical relationship?
options: One species benefits while the other is not significantly affected
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Commensalism benefits one species without a major effect on the other.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: In predation, the predator generally does what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Predators obtain food by capturing or consuming prey.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: An ecosystem includes a community of organisms and what else?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: An ecosystem includes living organisms and their physical environment.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which organisms form the first trophic level in most ecosystems?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Producers capture energy, commonly through photosynthesis.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which organisms break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Fungi and bacteria commonly act as decomposers.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Energy flow through an ecosystem is generally what?
options: Unidirectional, with energy lost as heat at each transfer
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Energy dissipates as heat and is not recycled like nutrients.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Lindeman's ten percent law describes approximately how much energy transferred from one trophic level to the next?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Only a small fraction, often approximated as 10%, passes to the next trophic level.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which ecological pyramid is always upright?
options: Pyramid of numbers in every case
Pyramid of biomass in every case
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Energy decreases at successive trophic levels.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Primary productivity refers to the rate at which producers do what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Primary productivity is the rate of biomass or organic matter production by producers.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which process is part of decomposition?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Decomposition includes fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralisation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: The gradual change in community composition over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Succession describes changes in ecological communities over time.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Unlike energy, nutrients in ecosystems generally do what?
options: Cycle between organisms and the environment
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Elements such as carbon and nitrogen cycle through biotic and abiotic components.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Biodiversity includes variation at genetic, species and what other level?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Biodiversity is considered at genetic, species and ecosystem levels.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: A species naturally restricted to a particular geographic region is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Endemic species have naturally limited geographic distributions.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Protecting species in their natural habitats is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: In situ conservation protects organisms within their natural ecosystems.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which is an example of ex situ conservation?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Seed banks preserve plant genetic material outside its natural habitat.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which organisation publishes the widely used Red List of Threatened Species?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The International Union for Conservation of Nature maintains the Red List.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: A biodiversity hotspot is identified by high endemism and what other feature?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Hotspots combine high endemism with substantial habitat loss.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: A species with a disproportionately large ecological effect relative to its abundance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Keystone species strongly influence ecosystem structure and function.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Breaking a continuous habitat into smaller, isolated patches is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Fragmentation can isolate populations and increase edge effects.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: A species is extinct when what condition is met?
options: It moves to another local habitat
Its population decreases for one season
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Extinction means the species no longer has living individuals.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which action supports long-term biodiversity conservation?
options: Protecting habitats and reducing major threats
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Habitat protection and threat reduction are central conservation measures.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which gas is a major contributor to human-driven global warming?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels and land-use change contribute to warming.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which chemicals historically contributed significantly to stratospheric ozone depletion?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: CFC-derived chlorine radicals can catalyse ozone destruction.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Excess nutrient enrichment of a water body that can cause algal blooms is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus can promote algal growth and oxygen depletion.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: An increase in concentration of persistent pollutants at higher trophic levels is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Persistent pollutants can accumulate through food chains.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Acid rain is mainly associated with atmospheric emissions of which gases?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Sulfur and nitrogen oxides form acids in the atmosphere.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which practice can reduce the amount of waste sent to landfills?
options: Mixing hazardous waste with food waste
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Waste prevention and recovery reduce landfill pressure.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Sound levels are commonly expressed in which unit?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Sound pressure levels are commonly expressed in decibels.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Which is a renewable energy source?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Solar energy is replenished naturally on human timescales.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: The build-up of a substance in an organism over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Bioaccumulation occurs when uptake exceeds elimination.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Establishing forest cover on land not recently forested is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Afforestation establishes tree cover on suitable land.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which part of a typical angiosperm stamen produces pollen grains?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The anther contains microsporangia where pollen grains develop.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The formation of microspores from pollen mother cells by meiosis is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Microsporogenesis produces haploid microspores by meiosis.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The outer wall of a pollen grain, called the exine, contains which highly resistant material?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Sporopollenin is highly resistant to chemical and biological degradation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The typical mature angiosperm embryo sac is usually described as having how many cells and nuclei?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The common Polygonum-type embryo sac has seven cells and eight nuclei.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Pollination places pollen on a receptive stigma.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Double fertilisation in angiosperms consists of which two events?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: One male gamete fuses with the egg; the other fuses with the polar nuclei/secondary nucleus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: In a typical angiosperm, the primary endosperm nucleus is usually what ploidy?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Triple fusion commonly produces a triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Seed formation without fertilisation is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Apomixis can produce seeds without the normal fertilisation process.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Development of a fruit without fertilisation is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Parthenocarpy results in fruit development without fertilisation, often producing seedless fruits.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is an example of an outbreeding device in flowering plants?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Dichogamy separates pollen release and stigma receptivity in time.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Who is known as the father of genetics?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mendel's pea-plant experiments established foundational principles of inheritance.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Alternative forms of a gene are called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Alleles are alternative versions of a gene at a locus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A cross that studies the inheritance of one pair of contrasting traits is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: A monohybrid cross follows one trait.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Mendel's law of segregation states that paired alleles separate during what process?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Alleles segregate during gamete formation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: In snapdragon, a red-flowered plant crossed with a white-flowered plant can produce pink offspring. This illustrates what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which human blood group phenotype illustrates codominance of IA and IB alleles?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Both A and B antigens are expressed in the AB phenotype.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: An individual with a dominant phenotype is crossed with a homozygous recessive individual to determine its genotype. This is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: A test cross helps distinguish homozygous dominant from heterozygous genotypes.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Haemophilia is commonly inherited as which type of trait?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Haemophilia A and B are commonly X-linked recessive disorders.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A sudden heritable change in genetic material is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mutations create new genetic variation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which chart is used to trace the inheritance of a trait through generations?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Pedigree analysis helps infer inheritance patterns in families.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which molecule stores hereditary information in most organisms?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: DNA is the hereditary material in most organisms.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A nucleotide consists of which components?
options: A pentose sugar, phosphate group and nitrogenous base
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Nucleotides are the building blocks of nucleic acids.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which base pairs with adenine in DNA?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Why is DNA replication described as semiconservative?
options: Each daughter DNA molecule contains one parental and one new strand
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Each daughter double helix retains one original strand.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Synthesis of RNA using DNA as a template is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Transcription copies information from DNA into RNA.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which cellular structure reads mRNA to synthesise a polypeptide?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Ribosomes translate mRNA codons into an amino-acid sequence.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A three-nucleotide sequence on mRNA is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Codons specify amino acids or translation termination.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which RNA carries amino acids to the ribosome during translation?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: tRNA delivers amino acids and pairs its anticodon with mRNA codons.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: In the lac operon, lactose or its derivative acts as what when present?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The inducer inactivates the repressor and permits transcription of structural genes.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which was a major aim of the Human Genome Project?
options: Sequencing and mapping the human genome
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The project aimed to identify and map human genes and determine DNA sequence.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Natural selection favours heritable traits that improve what in a particular environment?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Traits that improve survival and reproduction can become more common.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Fossils provide evidence about what?
options: Past life and evolutionary change through geological time
The exact DNA of every living species
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Fossils document organisms from earlier geological periods.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Organs with a common evolutionary origin but different functions are called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Homology supports common ancestry.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Wings of birds and insects are often cited as examples of what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: They perform similar functions but evolved independently.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Random changes in allele frequencies are generally strongest in which populations?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Random sampling has a larger effect in small populations.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Movement of alleles between populations due to migration and reproduction is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Gene flow transfers alleles among populations.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: For a gene with two alleles at frequencies p and q, what is the relationship under the Hardy-Weinberg model?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Allele frequencies sum to one for a two-allele locus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The formation of new species is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Speciation involves divergence and reproductive isolation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Evolution of multiple species from a common ancestor into different ecological niches is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Adaptive radiation is diversification from a common ancestor into different niches.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The spread of antibiotic resistance in bacteria is an example of evolution by what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Antibiotics select for resistant variants already present or arising by mutation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: An agent that causes disease is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Pathogens include certain bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Malaria is caused by which type of organism?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Plasmodium species are protozoan parasites that cause malaria.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Malaria is transmitted by the bite of an infected female mosquito of which genus?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium parasites.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Dengue is caused by which type of pathogen?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Dengue is caused by dengue viruses.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Tuberculosis is caused by which organism?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which cells differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Activated B cells can differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Vaccination primarily aims to generate what?
options: Immediate replacement of all white cells
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Vaccines stimulate immune responses and memory against specific pathogens.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Cancer is characterised by abnormal, uncontrolled what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Cancer involves uncontrolled cell growth and may invade other tissues.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: HIV primarily attacks which immune cells?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: HIV targets CD4-positive immune cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: An exaggerated immune response to a normally harmless substance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Allergy is a hypersensitivity response to an allergen.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which microbes help convert milk into curd?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Lactic acid bacteria ferment lactose and acidify milk.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which microorganism is used in bread-making and alcoholic fermentation?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Yeast ferments sugars and releases carbon dioxide and ethanol under suitable conditions.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Penicillin was discovered from a mould belonging to which genus?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Penicillium moulds produce penicillin compounds.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which microorganisms produce methane under anaerobic conditions in biogas plants?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Methanogens generate methane in anaerobic digesters.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Activated sludge treatment relies heavily on what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Microorganisms break down organic pollutants in wastewater.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Rhizobium bacteria commonly form nitrogen-fixing associations with which plants?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Rhizobium in legume root nodules fixes atmospheric nitrogen.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Mycorrhiza is an association between plant roots and what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mycorrhizal fungi can improve uptake of minerals such as phosphorus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Using living organisms to control pests is known as what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Biological control uses natural enemies or antagonists to reduce pests.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Biochemical oxygen demand is used as an indicator of what in water?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Higher BOD generally indicates greater oxygen demand from biodegradable matter.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Antibiotics are substances used to inhibit or kill susceptible what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Antibiotics act against bacteria and do not directly treat viral infections.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific DNA sequences and do what?
options: Cut DNA at or near those sequences
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sites.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which enzyme joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is the primary purpose of polymerase chain reaction?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: PCR produces many copies of a target DNA segment.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A small circular DNA molecule often used as a cloning vector is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Plasmids can carry inserted DNA into host cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Why are selectable markers used in cloning vectors?
options: To identify or select cells carrying the vector
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Selectable markers help distinguish transformed cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A bioreactor provides controlled conditions for what?
options: Biological production using cells or enzymes
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Bioreactors control factors such as pH, temperature and aeration.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Unlike energy, nutrients in ecosystems generally do what?
options: Cycle between organisms and the environment
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Elements such as carbon and nitrogen cycle through biotic and abiotic components.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Biodiversity includes variation at genetic, species and what other level?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Biodiversity is considered at genetic, species and ecosystem levels.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A species naturally restricted to a particular geographic region is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Endemic species have naturally limited geographic distributions.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Protecting species in their natural habitats is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: In situ conservation protects organisms within their natural ecosystems.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is an example of ex situ conservation?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Seed banks preserve plant genetic material outside its natural habitat.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which organisation publishes the widely used Red List of Threatened Species?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The International Union for Conservation of Nature maintains the Red List.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A biodiversity hotspot is identified by high endemism and what other feature?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Hotspots combine high endemism with substantial habitat loss.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A species with a disproportionately large ecological effect relative to its abundance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Keystone species strongly influence ecosystem structure and function.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Breaking a continuous habitat into smaller, isolated patches is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Fragmentation can isolate populations and increase edge effects.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A species is extinct when what condition is met?
options: It moves to another local habitat
Its population decreases for one season
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Extinction means the species no longer has living individuals.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which action supports long-term biodiversity conservation?
options: Protecting habitats and reducing major threats
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Habitat protection and threat reduction are central conservation measures.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which gas is a major contributor to human-driven global warming?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels and land-use change contribute to warming.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which chemicals historically contributed significantly to stratospheric ozone depletion?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: CFC-derived chlorine radicals can catalyse ozone destruction.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Excess nutrient enrichment of a water body that can cause algal blooms is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus can promote algal growth and oxygen depletion.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: An increase in concentration of persistent pollutants at higher trophic levels is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Persistent pollutants can accumulate through food chains.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Acid rain is mainly associated with atmospheric emissions of which gases?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Sulfur and nitrogen oxides form acids in the atmosphere.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which practice can reduce the amount of waste sent to landfills?
options: Mixing hazardous waste with food waste
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Waste prevention and recovery reduce landfill pressure.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Sound levels are commonly expressed in which unit?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Sound pressure levels are commonly expressed in decibels.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is a renewable energy source?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Solar energy is replenished naturally on human timescales.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: The build-up of a substance in an organism over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Bioaccumulation occurs when uptake exceeds elimination.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Establishing forest cover on land not recently forested is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Afforestation establishes tree cover on suitable land.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which part of a typical angiosperm stamen produces pollen grains?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The anther contains microsporangia where pollen grains develop.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: The formation of microspores from pollen mother cells by meiosis is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Microsporogenesis produces haploid microspores by meiosis.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: The outer wall of a pollen grain, called the exine, contains which highly resistant material?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Sporopollenin is highly resistant to chemical and biological degradation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: The typical mature angiosperm embryo sac is usually described as having how many cells and nuclei?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The common Polygonum-type embryo sac has seven cells and eight nuclei.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Pollination places pollen on a receptive stigma.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Double fertilisation in angiosperms consists of which two events?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: One male gamete fuses with the egg; the other fuses with the polar nuclei/secondary nucleus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: In a typical angiosperm, the primary endosperm nucleus is usually what ploidy?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Triple fusion commonly produces a triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Seed formation without fertilisation is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Apomixis can produce seeds without the normal fertilisation process.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Development of a fruit without fertilisation is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Parthenocarpy results in fruit development without fertilisation, often producing seedless fruits.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which is an example of an outbreeding device in flowering plants?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Dichogamy separates pollen release and stigma receptivity in time.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Who is known as the father of genetics?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mendel's pea-plant experiments established foundational principles of inheritance.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Alternative forms of a gene are called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Alleles are alternative versions of a gene at a locus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: A cross that studies the inheritance of one pair of contrasting traits is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: A monohybrid cross follows one trait.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Mendel's law of segregation states that paired alleles separate during what process?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Alleles segregate during gamete formation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: In snapdragon, a red-flowered plant crossed with a white-flowered plant can produce pink offspring. This illustrates what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which human blood group phenotype illustrates codominance of IA and IB alleles?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Both A and B antigens are expressed in the AB phenotype.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: An individual with a dominant phenotype is crossed with a homozygous recessive individual to determine its genotype. This is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: A test cross helps distinguish homozygous dominant from heterozygous genotypes.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Haemophilia is commonly inherited as which type of trait?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Haemophilia A and B are commonly X-linked recessive disorders.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: A sudden heritable change in genetic material is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mutations create new genetic variation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which chart is used to trace the inheritance of a trait through generations?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Pedigree analysis helps infer inheritance patterns in families.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which molecule stores hereditary information in most organisms?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: DNA is the hereditary material in most organisms.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: A nucleotide consists of which components?
options: A pentose sugar, phosphate group and nitrogenous base
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Nucleotides are the building blocks of nucleic acids.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which base pairs with adenine in DNA?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Why is DNA replication described as semiconservative?
options: Each daughter DNA molecule contains one parental and one new strand
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Each daughter double helix retains one original strand.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Synthesis of RNA using DNA as a template is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Transcription copies information from DNA into RNA.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which cellular structure reads mRNA to synthesise a polypeptide?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Ribosomes translate mRNA codons into an amino-acid sequence.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: A three-nucleotide sequence on mRNA is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Codons specify amino acids or translation termination.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which RNA carries amino acids to the ribosome during translation?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: tRNA delivers amino acids and pairs its anticodon with mRNA codons.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: In the lac operon, lactose or its derivative acts as what when present?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The inducer inactivates the repressor and permits transcription of structural genes.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which was a major aim of the Human Genome Project?
options: Sequencing and mapping the human genome
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The project aimed to identify and map human genes and determine DNA sequence.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Natural selection favours heritable traits that improve what in a particular environment?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Traits that improve survival and reproduction can become more common.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Fossils provide evidence about what?
options: Past life and evolutionary change through geological time
The exact DNA of every living species
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Fossils document organisms from earlier geological periods.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Organs with a common evolutionary origin but different functions are called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Homology supports common ancestry.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Wings of birds and insects are often cited as examples of what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: They perform similar functions but evolved independently.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Random changes in allele frequencies are generally strongest in which populations?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Random sampling has a larger effect in small populations.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Movement of alleles between populations due to migration and reproduction is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Gene flow transfers alleles among populations.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: For a gene with two alleles at frequencies p and q, what is the relationship under the Hardy-Weinberg model?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Allele frequencies sum to one for a two-allele locus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: The formation of new species is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Speciation involves divergence and reproductive isolation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Evolution of multiple species from a common ancestor into different ecological niches is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Adaptive radiation is diversification from a common ancestor into different niches.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: The spread of antibiotic resistance in bacteria is an example of evolution by what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Antibiotics select for resistant variants already present or arising by mutation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: An agent that causes disease is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Pathogens include certain bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Malaria is caused by which type of organism?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Plasmodium species are protozoan parasites that cause malaria.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Malaria is transmitted by the bite of an infected female mosquito of which genus?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium parasites.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Dengue is caused by which type of pathogen?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Dengue is caused by dengue viruses.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Tuberculosis is caused by which organism?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which cells differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Activated B cells can differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Vaccination primarily aims to generate what?
options: Immediate replacement of all white cells
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Vaccines stimulate immune responses and memory against specific pathogens.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Cancer is characterised by abnormal, uncontrolled what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Cancer involves uncontrolled cell growth and may invade other tissues.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: HIV primarily attacks which immune cells?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: HIV targets CD4-positive immune cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: An exaggerated immune response to a normally harmless substance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Allergy is a hypersensitivity response to an allergen.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which microbes help convert milk into curd?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Lactic acid bacteria ferment lactose and acidify milk.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which microorganism is used in bread-making and alcoholic fermentation?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Yeast ferments sugars and releases carbon dioxide and ethanol under suitable conditions.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Penicillin was discovered from a mould belonging to which genus?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Penicillium moulds produce penicillin compounds.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which microorganisms produce methane under anaerobic conditions in biogas plants?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Methanogens generate methane in anaerobic digesters.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Activated sludge treatment relies heavily on what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Microorganisms break down organic pollutants in wastewater.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Rhizobium bacteria commonly form nitrogen-fixing associations with which plants?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Rhizobium in legume root nodules fixes atmospheric nitrogen.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Mycorrhiza is an association between plant roots and what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mycorrhizal fungi can improve uptake of minerals such as phosphorus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Using living organisms to control pests is known as what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Biological control uses natural enemies or antagonists to reduce pests.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Biochemical oxygen demand is used as an indicator of what in water?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Higher BOD generally indicates greater oxygen demand from biodegradable matter.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Antibiotics are substances used to inhibit or kill susceptible what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Antibiotics act against bacteria and do not directly treat viral infections.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific DNA sequences and do what?
options: Cut DNA at or near those sequences
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sites.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which enzyme joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: What is the primary purpose of polymerase chain reaction?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: PCR produces many copies of a target DNA segment.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: A small circular DNA molecule often used as a cloning vector is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Plasmids can carry inserted DNA into host cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Why are selectable markers used in cloning vectors?
options: To identify or select cells carrying the vector
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Selectable markers help distinguish transformed cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: A bioreactor provides controlled conditions for what?
options: Biological production using cells or enzymes
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Bioreactors control factors such as pH, temperature and aeration.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: DNA fragments are separated during agarose gel electrophoresis mainly according to what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: DNA fragments migrate through the gel; smaller fragments usually move farther.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: DNA formed by joining genetic material from different sources is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Recombinant DNA combines DNA sequences from different sources.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which vector feature allows DNA replication to begin in a host cell?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The origin of replication is the site where replication machinery initiates copying.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: In genetic engineering, competent cells are cells capable of doing what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Competent cells are prepared to take up DNA.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Bt cotton contains genes derived from which bacterium?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Bt genes can enable plants to produce proteins toxic to certain insect pests.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: RNA interference can silence gene expression through which type of molecule?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: RNAi uses small RNA molecules to target and reduce specific RNA transcripts.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Gene therapy aims to treat disease by introducing or modifying what?
options: Genetic material or gene function in cells
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Gene therapy seeks to alter gene function or expression.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Recombinant human insulin is produced using which general technology?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Recombinant DNA methods can enable microbes to produce human insulin.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: An organism carrying introduced genetic material is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Transgenic organisms contain genetic material introduced through genetic engineering.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: ELISA commonly detects a target using specific binding between antigen and what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: ELISA uses antigen-antibody recognition and an enzyme-linked signal.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: PCR can help diagnose some infections by detecting what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: PCR can amplify pathogen-specific DNA or, with reverse transcription, RNA-derived targets.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Why is biosafety assessment important when releasing a genetically modified organism?
options: To assess potential risks to health and the environment
To guarantee zero risk without testing
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Risk assessment evaluates potential hazards and exposure pathways.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Golden rice was developed to increase the level of which nutrient precursor in rice endosperm?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Golden rice is engineered to accumulate beta-carotene, a provitamin A carotenoid.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: A patent related to a biological invention or process is commonly called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Biopatents concern qualifying biological inventions, subject to applicable law.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: A population consists of individuals of the same species living in what context?
options: The same area at the same time
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Population ecology studies members of a species sharing an area and time.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: The place where an organism lives is called its what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Habitat refers to the physical place an organism occupies.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: The ecological role and resource use of a species are described by its what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: A niche describes how a species uses resources and interacts with its environment.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: The maximum population size an environment can sustain over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Carrying capacity depends on resources and environmental conditions.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Under ideal conditions with unlimited resources, population growth may form which curve?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Exponential growth accelerates when limiting factors are absent.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Population growth that slows as it approaches carrying capacity is represented by which curve?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Logistic growth includes density-dependent limitation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: In mutualism, how are the two species affected?
options: One benefits and the other is always harmed
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mutualism is an interaction in which both partners benefit.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: In parasitism, which organism benefits while the other is harmed?
options: Parasite benefits and host is harmed
Host benefits and parasite is harmed
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Parasites obtain resources from hosts, often causing harm.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: In commensalism, what is the typical relationship?
options: One species benefits while the other is not significantly affected
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Commensalism benefits one species without a major effect on the other.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: In predation, the predator generally does what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Predators obtain food by capturing or consuming prey.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: An ecosystem includes a community of organisms and what else?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: An ecosystem includes living organisms and their physical environment.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which organisms form the first trophic level in most ecosystems?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Producers capture energy, commonly through photosynthesis.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which organisms break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Fungi and bacteria commonly act as decomposers.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Energy flow through an ecosystem is generally what?
options: Unidirectional, with energy lost as heat at each transfer
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Energy dissipates as heat and is not recycled like nutrients.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Lindeman's ten percent law describes approximately how much energy transferred from one trophic level to the next?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Only a small fraction, often approximated as 10%, passes to the next trophic level.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which ecological pyramid is always upright?
options: Pyramid of biomass in every case
Pyramid of numbers in every case
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Energy decreases at successive trophic levels.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Primary productivity refers to the rate at which producers do what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Primary productivity is the rate of biomass or organic matter production by producers.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Choose the best answer: Which process is part of decomposition?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Decomposition includes fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralisation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Succession describes changes in ecological communities over time.

CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Elements such as carbon and nitrogen cycle through biotic and abiotic components.
