CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Dichogamy separates pollen release and stigma receptivity in time.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Who is known as the father of genetics?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mendel's pea-plant experiments established foundational principles of inheritance.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Alternative forms of a gene are called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Alleles are alternative versions of a gene at a locus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: A cross that studies the inheritance of one pair of contrasting traits is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: A monohybrid cross follows one trait.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Mendel's law of segregation states that paired alleles separate during what process?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Alleles segregate during gamete formation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: In snapdragon, a red-flowered plant crossed with a white-flowered plant can produce pink offspring. This illustrates what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which human blood group phenotype illustrates codominance of IA and IB alleles?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Both A and B antigens are expressed in the AB phenotype.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: An individual with a dominant phenotype is crossed with a homozygous recessive individual to determine its genotype. This is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: A test cross helps distinguish homozygous dominant from heterozygous genotypes.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Haemophilia is commonly inherited as which type of trait?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Haemophilia A and B are commonly X-linked recessive disorders.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: A sudden heritable change in genetic material is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mutations create new genetic variation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which chart is used to trace the inheritance of a trait through generations?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Pedigree analysis helps infer inheritance patterns in families.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which molecule stores hereditary information in most organisms?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: DNA is the hereditary material in most organisms.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: A nucleotide consists of which components?
options: A pentose sugar, phosphate group and nitrogenous base
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Nucleotides are the building blocks of nucleic acids.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which base pairs with adenine in DNA?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Why is DNA replication described as semiconservative?
options: Each daughter DNA molecule contains one parental and one new strand
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Each daughter double helix retains one original strand.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Synthesis of RNA using DNA as a template is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Transcription copies information from DNA into RNA.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which cellular structure reads mRNA to synthesise a polypeptide?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Ribosomes translate mRNA codons into an amino-acid sequence.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: A three-nucleotide sequence on mRNA is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Codons specify amino acids or translation termination.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which RNA carries amino acids to the ribosome during translation?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: tRNA delivers amino acids and pairs its anticodon with mRNA codons.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: In the lac operon, lactose or its derivative acts as what when present?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The inducer inactivates the repressor and permits transcription of structural genes.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which was a major aim of the Human Genome Project?
options: Sequencing and mapping the human genome
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The project aimed to identify and map human genes and determine DNA sequence.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Natural selection favours heritable traits that improve what in a particular environment?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Traits that improve survival and reproduction can become more common.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Fossils provide evidence about what?
options: Past life and evolutionary change through geological time
The exact DNA of every living species
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Fossils document organisms from earlier geological periods.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Organs with a common evolutionary origin but different functions are called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Homology supports common ancestry.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Wings of birds and insects are often cited as examples of what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: They perform similar functions but evolved independently.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Random changes in allele frequencies are generally strongest in which populations?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Random sampling has a larger effect in small populations.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Movement of alleles between populations due to migration and reproduction is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Gene flow transfers alleles among populations.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: For a gene with two alleles at frequencies p and q, what is the relationship under the Hardy-Weinberg model?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Allele frequencies sum to one for a two-allele locus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: The formation of new species is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Speciation involves divergence and reproductive isolation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Evolution of multiple species from a common ancestor into different ecological niches is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Adaptive radiation is diversification from a common ancestor into different niches.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: The spread of antibiotic resistance in bacteria is an example of evolution by what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Antibiotics select for resistant variants already present or arising by mutation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: An agent that causes disease is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Pathogens include certain bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Malaria is caused by which type of organism?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Plasmodium species are protozoan parasites that cause malaria.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Malaria is transmitted by the bite of an infected female mosquito of which genus?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium parasites.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Dengue is caused by which type of pathogen?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Dengue is caused by dengue viruses.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Tuberculosis is caused by which organism?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which cells differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Activated B cells can differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Vaccination primarily aims to generate what?
options: Immediate replacement of all white cells
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Vaccines stimulate immune responses and memory against specific pathogens.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Cancer is characterised by abnormal, uncontrolled what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Cancer involves uncontrolled cell growth and may invade other tissues.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: HIV primarily attacks which immune cells?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: HIV targets CD4-positive immune cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: An exaggerated immune response to a normally harmless substance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Allergy is a hypersensitivity response to an allergen.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which microbes help convert milk into curd?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Lactic acid bacteria ferment lactose and acidify milk.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which microorganism is used in bread-making and alcoholic fermentation?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Yeast ferments sugars and releases carbon dioxide and ethanol under suitable conditions.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Penicillin was discovered from a mould belonging to which genus?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Penicillium moulds produce penicillin compounds.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which microorganisms produce methane under anaerobic conditions in biogas plants?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Methanogens generate methane in anaerobic digesters.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Activated sludge treatment relies heavily on what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Microorganisms break down organic pollutants in wastewater.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Rhizobium bacteria commonly form nitrogen-fixing associations with which plants?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Rhizobium in legume root nodules fixes atmospheric nitrogen.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Mycorrhiza is an association between plant roots and what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mycorrhizal fungi can improve uptake of minerals such as phosphorus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Using living organisms to control pests is known as what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Biological control uses natural enemies or antagonists to reduce pests.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Biochemical oxygen demand is used as an indicator of what in water?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Higher BOD generally indicates greater oxygen demand from biodegradable matter.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Antibiotics are substances used to inhibit or kill susceptible what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Antibiotics act against bacteria and do not directly treat viral infections.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific DNA sequences and do what?
options: Cut DNA at or near those sequences
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sites.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which enzyme joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: What is the primary purpose of polymerase chain reaction?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: PCR produces many copies of a target DNA segment.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: A small circular DNA molecule often used as a cloning vector is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Plasmids can carry inserted DNA into host cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Why are selectable markers used in cloning vectors?
options: To identify or select cells carrying the vector
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Selectable markers help distinguish transformed cells.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: A bioreactor provides controlled conditions for what?
options: Biological production using cells or enzymes
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Bioreactors control factors such as pH, temperature and aeration.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: DNA fragments are separated during agarose gel electrophoresis mainly according to what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: DNA fragments migrate through the gel; smaller fragments usually move farther.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: DNA formed by joining genetic material from different sources is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Recombinant DNA combines DNA sequences from different sources.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which vector feature allows DNA replication to begin in a host cell?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The origin of replication is the site where replication machinery initiates copying.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: In genetic engineering, competent cells are cells capable of doing what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Competent cells are prepared to take up DNA.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Bt cotton contains genes derived from which bacterium?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Bt genes can enable plants to produce proteins toxic to certain insect pests.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: RNA interference can silence gene expression through which type of molecule?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: RNAi uses small RNA molecules to target and reduce specific RNA transcripts.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Gene therapy aims to treat disease by introducing or modifying what?
options: Genetic material or gene function in cells
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Gene therapy seeks to alter gene function or expression.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Recombinant human insulin is produced using which general technology?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Recombinant DNA methods can enable microbes to produce human insulin.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: An organism carrying introduced genetic material is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Transgenic organisms contain genetic material introduced through genetic engineering.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: ELISA commonly detects a target using specific binding between antigen and what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: ELISA uses antigen-antibody recognition and an enzyme-linked signal.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: PCR can help diagnose some infections by detecting what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: PCR can amplify pathogen-specific DNA or, with reverse transcription, RNA-derived targets.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Why is biosafety assessment important when releasing a genetically modified organism?
options: To assess potential risks to health and the environment
To guarantee zero risk without testing
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Risk assessment evaluates potential hazards and exposure pathways.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Golden rice was developed to increase the level of which nutrient precursor in rice endosperm?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Golden rice is engineered to accumulate beta-carotene, a provitamin A carotenoid.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: A patent related to a biological invention or process is commonly called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Biopatents concern qualifying biological inventions, subject to applicable law.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: A population consists of individuals of the same species living in what context?
options: The same area at the same time
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Population ecology studies members of a species sharing an area and time.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: The place where an organism lives is called its what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Habitat refers to the physical place an organism occupies.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: The ecological role and resource use of a species are described by its what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: A niche describes how a species uses resources and interacts with its environment.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: The maximum population size an environment can sustain over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Carrying capacity depends on resources and environmental conditions.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Under ideal conditions with unlimited resources, population growth may form which curve?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Exponential growth accelerates when limiting factors are absent.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Population growth that slows as it approaches carrying capacity is represented by which curve?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Logistic growth includes density-dependent limitation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: In mutualism, how are the two species affected?
options: One benefits and the other is always harmed
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mutualism is an interaction in which both partners benefit.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: In parasitism, which organism benefits while the other is harmed?
options: Parasite benefits and host is harmed
Host benefits and parasite is harmed
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Parasites obtain resources from hosts, often causing harm.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: In commensalism, what is the typical relationship?
options: One species benefits while the other is not significantly affected
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Commensalism benefits one species without a major effect on the other.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: In predation, the predator generally does what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Predators obtain food by capturing or consuming prey.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: An ecosystem includes a community of organisms and what else?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: An ecosystem includes living organisms and their physical environment.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which organisms form the first trophic level in most ecosystems?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Producers capture energy, commonly through photosynthesis.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which organisms break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Fungi and bacteria commonly act as decomposers.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Energy flow through an ecosystem is generally what?
options: Unidirectional, with energy lost as heat at each transfer
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Energy dissipates as heat and is not recycled like nutrients.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Lindeman's ten percent law describes approximately how much energy transferred from one trophic level to the next?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Only a small fraction, often approximated as 10%, passes to the next trophic level.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which ecological pyramid is always upright?
options: Pyramid of biomass in every case
Pyramid of numbers in every case
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Energy decreases at successive trophic levels.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Primary productivity refers to the rate at which producers do what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Primary productivity is the rate of biomass or organic matter production by producers.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which process is part of decomposition?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Decomposition includes fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralisation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: The gradual change in community composition over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Succession describes changes in ecological communities over time.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Unlike energy, nutrients in ecosystems generally do what?
options: Cycle between organisms and the environment
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Elements such as carbon and nitrogen cycle through biotic and abiotic components.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Biodiversity includes variation at genetic, species and what other level?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Biodiversity is considered at genetic, species and ecosystem levels.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: A species naturally restricted to a particular geographic region is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Endemic species have naturally limited geographic distributions.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Protecting species in their natural habitats is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: In situ conservation protects organisms within their natural ecosystems.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which is an example of ex situ conservation?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Seed banks preserve plant genetic material outside its natural habitat.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which organisation publishes the widely used Red List of Threatened Species?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The International Union for Conservation of Nature maintains the Red List.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: A biodiversity hotspot is identified by high endemism and what other feature?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Hotspots combine high endemism with substantial habitat loss.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: A species with a disproportionately large ecological effect relative to its abundance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Keystone species strongly influence ecosystem structure and function.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Breaking a continuous habitat into smaller, isolated patches is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Fragmentation can isolate populations and increase edge effects.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: A species is extinct when what condition is met?
options: It moves to another local habitat
Its population decreases for one season
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Extinction means the species no longer has living individuals.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which action supports long-term biodiversity conservation?
options: Protecting habitats and reducing major threats
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Habitat protection and threat reduction are central conservation measures.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which gas is a major contributor to human-driven global warming?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels and land-use change contribute to warming.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which chemicals historically contributed significantly to stratospheric ozone depletion?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: CFC-derived chlorine radicals can catalyse ozone destruction.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Excess nutrient enrichment of a water body that can cause algal blooms is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus can promote algal growth and oxygen depletion.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: An increase in concentration of persistent pollutants at higher trophic levels is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Persistent pollutants can accumulate through food chains.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Acid rain is mainly associated with atmospheric emissions of which gases?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Sulfur and nitrogen oxides form acids in the atmosphere.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which practice can reduce the amount of waste sent to landfills?
options: Mixing hazardous waste with food waste
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Waste prevention and recovery reduce landfill pressure.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Sound levels are commonly expressed in which unit?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Sound pressure levels are commonly expressed in decibels.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Which is a renewable energy source?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Solar energy is replenished naturally on human timescales.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: The build-up of a substance in an organism over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Bioaccumulation occurs when uptake exceeds elimination.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Quick review: Establishing forest cover on land not recently forested is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Afforestation establishes tree cover on suitable land.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: Which part of a typical angiosperm stamen produces pollen grains?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The anther contains microsporangia where pollen grains develop.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: The formation of microspores from pollen mother cells by meiosis is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Microsporogenesis produces haploid microspores by meiosis.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: The outer wall of a pollen grain, called the exine, contains which highly resistant material?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Sporopollenin is highly resistant to chemical and biological degradation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: The typical mature angiosperm embryo sac is usually described as having how many cells and nuclei?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The common Polygonum-type embryo sac has seven cells and eight nuclei.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Pollination places pollen on a receptive stigma.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: Double fertilisation in angiosperms consists of which two events?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: One male gamete fuses with the egg; the other fuses with the polar nuclei/secondary nucleus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: In a typical angiosperm, the primary endosperm nucleus is usually what ploidy?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Triple fusion commonly produces a triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: Seed formation without fertilisation is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Apomixis can produce seeds without the normal fertilisation process.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: Development of a fruit without fertilisation is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Parthenocarpy results in fruit development without fertilisation, often producing seedless fruits.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: Which is an example of an outbreeding device in flowering plants?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Dichogamy separates pollen release and stigma receptivity in time.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: Who is known as the father of genetics?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mendel's pea-plant experiments established foundational principles of inheritance.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: Alternative forms of a gene are called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Alleles are alternative versions of a gene at a locus.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: A cross that studies the inheritance of one pair of contrasting traits is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: A monohybrid cross follows one trait.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: Mendel's law of segregation states that paired alleles separate during what process?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Alleles segregate during gamete formation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: In snapdragon, a red-flowered plant crossed with a white-flowered plant can produce pink offspring. This illustrates what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: The heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: Which human blood group phenotype illustrates codominance of IA and IB alleles?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Both A and B antigens are expressed in the AB phenotype.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: An individual with a dominant phenotype is crossed with a homozygous recessive individual to determine its genotype. This is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: A test cross helps distinguish homozygous dominant from heterozygous genotypes.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: Haemophilia is commonly inherited as which type of trait?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Haemophilia A and B are commonly X-linked recessive disorders.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: A sudden heritable change in genetic material is called what?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Mutations create new genetic variation.

CBSE 12 - Botany.q: Revision check: Which chart is used to trace the inheritance of a trait through generations?
CBSE 12 - Botany.why: Pedigree analysis helps infer inheritance patterns in families.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: Which concentration term is defined as moles of solute per litre of solution?
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: Molarity is the amount of solute in moles divided by solution volume in litres.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: Molality is expressed as moles of solute per:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: Molality uses the mass of solvent in kilograms.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: Which concentration term is independent of temperature, assuming composition does not change?
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: Molality is based on mass, which does not change appreciably with temperature.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: The sum of mole fractions of all components in a solution is:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: The mole fractions of all components sum to one.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: Raoult's law for a volatile component states that its partial vapour pressure equals:
options: the total pressure times its molar mass
its mass fraction divided by pressure
its mole fraction times its pure vapour pressure
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: For an ideal solution, pᵢ = xᵢpᵢ°.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: An ideal solution obeys Raoult's law:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: Ideal solutions obey Raoult's law at all compositions.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: A positive deviation from Raoult's law generally means A–B interactions are:
options: weaker than the average A–A and B–B interactions
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: Weaker unlike interactions favour escape to vapour and raise vapour pressure.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: Which is a colligative property?
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: Colligative properties depend on the number of solute particles.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: Adding a non-volatile solute to a solvent generally causes its freezing point to:
options: become equal to its boiling point
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: Freezing-point depression is a colligative property.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: For dilute solutions, osmotic pressure is represented by:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: For a dilute solution, osmotic pressure follows π = CRT.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: The van't Hoff factor accounts for:
options: association or dissociation of solute particles
the density of the solvent only
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: The van't Hoff factor adjusts colligative properties for the actual number of particles.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: Henry's law relates gas solubility in a liquid to:
options: the atomic number of the solvent
the partial pressure of the gas
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: At a fixed temperature, gas solubility is proportional to its partial pressure.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: Which solution has the highest boiling point at equal molality, assuming complete dissociation where applicable?
options: All solutions must have the same boiling point
A solution producing the greatest number of solute particles
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: Boiling-point elevation depends on the effective number of dissolved particles.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: Osmosis is the net movement of solvent through a semipermeable membrane from:
options: higher solute concentration to lower solute concentration only
lower solute concentration to higher solute concentration
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: Solvent tends to move toward the more concentrated solution.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: For a dilute solution, relative lowering of vapour pressure is equal to the mole fraction of:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: For a non-volatile solute, (p° − p)/p° = xsolute.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: 1 mol of solute is dissolved to make 10 L of solution. What is the molarity?
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: Molarity = moles of solute / volume of solution in litres.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: 2 mol of solute is dissolved to make 10 L of solution. What is the molarity?
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: Molarity = moles of solute / volume of solution in litres.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: 5 mol of solute is dissolved to make 10 L of solution. What is the molarity?
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: Molarity = moles of solute / volume of solution in litres.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.q: 10 mol of solute is dissolved to make 10 L of solution. What is the molarity?
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: Molarity = moles of solute / volume of solution in litres.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Solutions.why: Molarity = moles of solute / volume of solution in litres.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Fructose is classified as a:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Fructose is a six-carbon ketose.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Sucrose is composed of:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Sucrose is a disaccharide of glucose and fructose.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: The storage polysaccharide in animals is:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Animals store glucose mainly as glycogen.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Cellulose is a structural component of:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Cellulose provides structural support in plant cell walls.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: A peptide bond links:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Peptide bonds connect amino acids in proteins.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: The primary structure of a protein refers to its:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Primary structure is the linear sequence of amino acid residues.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Enzymes are biological catalysts that generally:
options: are consumed as the main reactant
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Enzymes lower activation energy and are not consumed overall.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: DNA contains which sugar?
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: DNA contains deoxyribose; RNA contains ribose.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: RNA contains which nitrogenous base in place of thymine?
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: RNA uses uracil where DNA uses thymine.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Vitamin C is also known as:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Denaturation of a protein usually disrupts its:
options: peptide bonds completely in all cases
amino acid sequence in every case
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Denaturation commonly disrupts secondary and tertiary structures without cleaving the primary sequence.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Which sugar is a reducing disaccharide?
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Lactose has a free anomeric carbon and is a reducing sugar.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: The peptide bond has the linkage:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: A peptide bond is an amide linkage between amino acids.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: The basic monomer unit of nucleic acids is a:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: DNA and RNA are polymers of nucleotides.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Vitamin D is important for regulation of:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Vitamin D supports calcium and phosphate homeostasis.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Which monosaccharide is a reducing sugar?
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Glucose has a free anomeric centre in equilibrium with an open-chain form.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: The secondary structure of proteins includes:
options: only the number of peptide bonds
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Hydrogen bonding stabilises common secondary structures.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Vitamin A is important for:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Vitamin A is required for normal vision and epithelial function.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: DNA bases pair specifically as:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine and guanine with cytosine.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Maltose is composed of:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Maltose is a disaccharide of two glucose units.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Starch is a storage polysaccharide in:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Plants store glucose in the form of starch.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Protein denaturation usually does not break the:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Denaturation disrupts higher-order folding while often preserving peptide bonds.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: RNA differs from DNA in that RNA usually contains:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: RNA contains ribose and uracil; DNA contains deoxyribose and thymine.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Vitamin B₁ is also known as:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Thiamine is vitamin B₁.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Which polysaccharide is made of β-D-glucose units and is indigestible by humans?
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Cellulose has β(1→4) linkages that humans cannot digest.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: The bond joining two monosaccharide units is called a:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Disaccharides are formed through glycosidic linkages.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: Which molecule carries genetic information in most organisms?
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: DNA is the principal hereditary material in most organisms.

CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.q: The monomers of proteins are:
CBSE 12 - Chemistry - Biomolecules.why: Proteins are polymers of amino acids.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: The production of sperm cells is called what?

CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Vasectomy blocks or cuts the vas deferens.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Tubectomy blocks or cuts the fallopian tubes.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which action helps reduce the risk of sexually transmitted infections?
options: Correct condom use and appropriate testing
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Prevention includes barrier protection, testing and timely medical care.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Amniocentesis involves sampling which fluid for certain prenatal tests?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Amniotic fluid may contain foetal cells useful for selected diagnostic tests.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: What is the most appropriate next step when a couple has concerns about infertility?
options: Seek assessment from a qualified healthcare professional
Assume one partner is always responsible
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Infertility may have multiple causes and should be evaluated appropriately.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which technique involves placing processed semen into the female reproductive tract?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Artificial insemination introduces semen into the reproductive tract by a medical procedure.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: A gene is best described as what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Genes are DNA sequences that contribute to functional products and inherited traits.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Alternative forms of the same gene are called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Alleles occupy corresponding loci and can contribute to variation.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: The genetic constitution of an organism for a trait is its what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Genotype refers to genetic makeup.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: The observable characteristics of an organism are called its what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Phenotype reflects genotype and environmental influences.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which ABO blood group phenotype expresses both A and B antigens on red blood cells?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: The AB phenotype expresses both A and B antigens.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: In the human ABO blood group system, IA and IB alleles show what relationship?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Both IA and IB are expressed in the AB phenotype.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: A gene with more than two alternative forms in a population is said to have what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: A population may contain multiple alleles, though a diploid individual carries at most two.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: The Rh-positive phenotype commonly reflects the presence of which red-cell antigen?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: The D antigen is the major antigen used in routine Rh classification.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: A heritable change in DNA sequence is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Mutations can create new genetic variants.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which chart is used to trace inheritance of a trait through family generations?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Pedigree charts help analyse inheritance patterns in families.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which molecule is the principal hereditary material in most organisms?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: DNA stores hereditary information in most organisms.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which components make up a nucleotide?
options: Sugar, phosphate group and nitrogenous base
Amino acid and fatty acid only
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: A nucleotide consists of a pentose sugar, phosphate group and nitrogenous base.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which base pairs with adenine in DNA?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which nitrogenous base occurs in RNA in place of thymine?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: RNA typically contains uracil instead of thymine.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Why is DNA replication described as semiconservative?
options: Each daughter molecule contains one parental and one newly synthesised strand
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Each daughter double helix retains one original strand.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: The synthesis of RNA using DNA as a template is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Transcription produces RNA from a DNA template.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: The process by which ribosomes use mRNA to synthesise a polypeptide is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Translation converts mRNA codon information into an amino-acid sequence.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: A sequence of three nucleotides in mRNA that specifies an amino acid or stop signal is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Codons are read in triplets during translation.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which RNA molecule carries amino acids to the ribosome?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: tRNA carries amino acids and pairs its anticodon with an mRNA codon.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: DNA fingerprinting commonly compares which type of variation?
options: Variable DNA regions such as STRs
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Variable DNA markers can help distinguish individuals.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Natural selection acts on heritable variation that affects what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Individuals with advantageous heritable traits may leave more offspring.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: A heritable feature that improves reproductive success in a particular environment is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Adaptations can increase fitness in a given environment.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, what is the relationship between allele frequencies p and q for a two-allele locus?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: For two alleles, their frequencies sum to one.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Random changes in allele frequencies are especially influential in which populations?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Sampling effects can cause strong random changes in small populations.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Movement of alleles between populations through migration and reproduction is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Gene flow transfers genetic variants between populations.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Fossils provide evidence about what?
options: Exact genotype of every living organism
Past life and changes through geological time
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Fossils document organisms and evolutionary changes across geological time.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Structures with a common evolutionary origin but possibly different functions are called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Homologous structures support common ancestry.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Structures that perform similar functions but evolved independently are called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Analogy often results from convergent evolution.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: The formation of new species is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Speciation occurs when populations diverge and become reproductively isolated.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: The spread of antibiotic resistance in bacteria is an example of evolution by what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Antibiotics select for resistant variants.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: An organism or agent that can cause disease is called a what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Pathogens include certain bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Malaria is caused by which genus of protozoan parasites?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Plasmodium species cause malaria.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Malaria is transmitted by the bite of an infected female mosquito of which genus?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Dengue is caused by which type of pathogen?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Dengue is caused by dengue viruses.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Tuberculosis is caused by which organism?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which cells differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Activated B cells can differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Vaccination primarily aims to generate what?
options: Immediate replacement of all white cells
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Vaccines stimulate immune responses and memory against specific pathogens.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Cancer is characterised by abnormal, uncontrolled what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Cancer involves uncontrolled cell growth and may invade other tissues.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: HIV primarily attacks which immune cells?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: HIV targets CD4-positive immune cells.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: An exaggerated immune response to a normally harmless substance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Allergies are hypersensitivity responses to specific allergens.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which microbes help convert milk into curd?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Lactic acid bacteria ferment lactose and acidify milk.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which microorganism is widely used in bread-making and alcoholic fermentation?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Yeast ferments sugars under suitable conditions.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Penicillin was discovered from a mould belonging to which genus?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Penicillium moulds produce penicillin compounds.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which microorganisms produce methane under anaerobic conditions in biogas plants?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Methanogens generate methane in anaerobic digesters.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Activated sludge treatment relies heavily on what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Microorganisms break down organic pollutants in wastewater.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Rhizobium bacteria commonly form nitrogen-fixing associations with which plants?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Rhizobium in legume root nodules fixes atmospheric nitrogen.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Mycorrhiza is an association between plant roots and what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Mycorrhizal fungi can improve uptake of minerals.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Using living organisms to manage pests is known as what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Biological control uses natural enemies or antagonists to reduce pests.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Biochemical oxygen demand is used as an indicator of what in water?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Higher BOD generally indicates greater oxygen demand from biodegradable matter.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Antibiotics are primarily used against susceptible infections caused by what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Antibiotics act against bacteria and do not directly treat viral infections.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific DNA sequences and do what?
options: Cut DNA at or near those sequences
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sites.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which enzyme joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: What is the main purpose of polymerase chain reaction?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: PCR produces many copies of a target DNA segment.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: A small circular DNA molecule often used as a cloning vector is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Plasmids can carry inserted DNA into host cells.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Why are selectable markers used in cloning vectors?
options: To identify or select cells carrying the vector
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Selectable markers help distinguish transformed cells.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: A bioreactor provides controlled conditions for what?
options: Biological production using cells or enzymes
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Bioreactors control pH, temperature, aeration and other conditions.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: DNA fragments are separated during agarose gel electrophoresis mainly according to what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Smaller DNA fragments usually move farther through agarose gel.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: DNA formed by joining genetic material from different sources is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Recombinant DNA combines sequences from different sources.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which vector feature allows DNA replication to begin in a host cell?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: The origin of replication is where replication machinery initiates copying.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: In genetic engineering, competent cells are capable of doing what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Competent cells are prepared to take up DNA.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Bt cotton contains genes derived from which bacterium?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Bt genes can enable plants to produce proteins toxic to certain insect pests.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: RNA interference can silence gene expression through which type of molecule?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: RNA interference uses small RNA molecules to reduce specific RNA transcripts.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Gene therapy aims to treat disease by introducing or modifying what?
options: Genetic material or gene function in cells
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Gene therapy seeks to alter gene function or expression.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Recombinant human insulin can be produced using which general technology?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Recombinant DNA methods enable microbes to produce human insulin.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: An organism carrying introduced genetic material is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Transgenic organisms contain introduced genetic material.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: ELISA commonly detects a target using specific binding between antigen and what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: ELISA uses antigen-antibody recognition and an enzyme-linked signal.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: PCR can help diagnose some infections by detecting what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: PCR amplifies pathogen-specific nucleic acid targets.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Why is biosafety assessment important before releasing a genetically modified organism?
options: To guarantee zero risk without testing
To assess potential risks to health and the environment
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Risk assessment evaluates potential hazards and exposure pathways.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Golden rice was developed to increase which nutrient precursor in rice endosperm?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Golden rice is engineered to accumulate beta-carotene, a provitamin A carotenoid.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: A patent related to a biological invention or process is commonly called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Biopatents concern qualifying biological inventions subject to applicable law.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: A population consists of individuals of the same species living in what context?
options: The same area at the same time
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Population ecology studies members of a species sharing an area and time.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: The place where an organism lives is called its what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Habitat refers to the physical place an organism occupies.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: The ecological role and resource use of a species are described by its what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: A niche describes how a species uses resources and interacts with its environment.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: The maximum population size an environment can sustain over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Carrying capacity depends on resources and environmental conditions.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Under ideal conditions with unlimited resources, population growth may form which curve?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Exponential growth accelerates when limiting factors are absent.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Population growth that slows as it approaches carrying capacity is represented by which curve?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Logistic growth includes density-dependent limitation.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: In mutualism, how are the two species affected?
options: One benefits and the other is always harmed
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Mutualism is an interaction in which both partners benefit.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: In parasitism, which organism benefits while the other is harmed?
options: Parasite benefits and host is harmed
Host benefits and parasite is harmed
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Parasites obtain resources from hosts, often causing harm.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: In commensalism, what is the typical relationship?
options: One species benefits while the other is not significantly affected
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Commensalism benefits one species without a major effect on the other.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: In predation, the predator generally does what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Predators obtain food by capturing or consuming prey.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: An ecosystem includes a community of organisms and what else?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: An ecosystem includes living organisms and their physical environment.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which organisms form the first trophic level in most ecosystems?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Producers capture energy, commonly through photosynthesis.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which organisms break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Fungi and bacteria commonly act as decomposers.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Energy flow through an ecosystem is generally what?
options: Unidirectional, with energy lost as heat at each transfer
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Energy dissipates as heat and is not recycled like nutrients.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Lindeman's ten percent law describes approximately how much energy transferred from one trophic level to the next?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Only a small fraction, often approximated as 10%, passes to the next trophic level.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which ecological pyramid is always upright?
options: Pyramid of numbers in every case
Pyramid of biomass in every case
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Energy decreases at successive trophic levels.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Primary productivity refers to the rate at which producers do what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Primary productivity is the rate of biomass or organic matter production.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which process is part of decomposition?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Decomposition includes fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralisation.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: The gradual change in community composition over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Succession describes changes in ecological communities over time.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Unlike energy, nutrients in ecosystems generally do what?
options: Cycle between organisms and the environment
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Elements such as carbon and nitrogen cycle through biotic and abiotic components.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Biodiversity includes variation at genetic, species and what other level?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Biodiversity is considered at genetic, species and ecosystem levels.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: A species naturally restricted to a particular geographic region is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Endemic species have naturally limited geographic distributions.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Protecting species in their natural habitats is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: In situ conservation protects organisms within natural ecosystems.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which is an example of ex situ conservation?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Seed banks preserve plant genetic material outside its natural habitat.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which organisation publishes the widely used Red List of Threatened Species?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: The International Union for Conservation of Nature maintains the Red List.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: A biodiversity hotspot is identified by high endemism and what other feature?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Hotspots combine high endemism with substantial habitat loss.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: A species with a disproportionately large ecological effect relative to its abundance is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Keystone species strongly influence ecosystem structure and function.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Breaking a continuous habitat into smaller, isolated patches is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Fragmentation can isolate populations and increase edge effects.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: A species is extinct when what condition is met?
options: It moves to another local habitat
Its population decreases for one season
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Extinction means the species no longer has living individuals.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which action supports long-term biodiversity conservation?

CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Habitat protection and threat reduction are central conservation measures.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which gas is a major contributor to human-driven global warming?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels and land-use change contribute to warming.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which chemicals historically contributed significantly to stratospheric ozone depletion?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: CFC-derived chlorine radicals can catalyse ozone destruction.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Excess nutrient enrichment of a water body that can cause algal blooms is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus can promote algal growth and oxygen depletion.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: An increase in concentration of persistent pollutants at higher trophic levels is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Persistent pollutants can accumulate through food chains.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Acid rain is mainly associated with atmospheric emissions of which gases?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Sulfur and nitrogen oxides form acids in the atmosphere.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which practice can reduce the amount of waste sent to landfills?
options: Mixing hazardous waste with food waste
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Waste prevention and recovery reduce landfill pressure.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Sound levels are commonly expressed in which unit?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Sound pressure levels are commonly expressed in decibels.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Which is a renewable energy source?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Solar energy is replenished naturally on human timescales.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: The build-up of a substance in an organism over time is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Bioaccumulation occurs when uptake exceeds elimination.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Establishing forest cover on land not recently forested is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Afforestation establishes tree cover on suitable land.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Revision check: The production of sperm cells is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Spermatogenesis occurs in the seminiferous tubules of the testes.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which testicular cells secrete testosterone?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Leydig cells, located between seminiferous tubules, secrete androgens.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Choose the best answer: Which cells support and nourish developing sperm cells in seminiferous tubules?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Sertoli cells support developing germ cells.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Quick review: The formation of female gametes is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Oogenesis is the process of forming ova.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Revision check: The release of a secondary oocyte from a mature ovarian follicle is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Ovulation releases a secondary oocyte from the ovary.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which structure forms from the ruptured follicle after ovulation?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: The corpus luteum secretes progesterone.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Choose the best answer: Where does fertilisation normally occur in humans?

CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Human fertilisation normally occurs at the ampullary-isthmic junction of the oviduct.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Quick review: The attachment of the blastocyst to the uterine endometrium is called what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Implantation embeds the blastocyst in the uterine lining.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Revision check: Which temporary organ facilitates exchange of nutrients, gases and wastes between mother and foetus?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: The placenta supports exchange and also functions as an endocrine tissue.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which hormone primarily stimulates milk production after childbirth?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Prolactin stimulates milk synthesis; oxytocin helps milk ejection.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Choose the best answer: What is the main purpose of contraceptive methods?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Contraception helps prevent unintended pregnancy.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Quick review: Which barrier method can also reduce the transmission risk of many sexually transmitted infections?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Correct condom use reduces pregnancy and STI transmission risk.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: Revision check: Copper-releasing intrauterine devices are primarily used to prevent what?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Copper IUDs interfere with sperm function and reduce the chance of fertilisation.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: In which assisted reproductive technique is fertilisation initiated outside the body?
CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: IVF involves fertilising an oocyte outside the body before embryo transfer.

CBSE 12 - Zoology.why: Vasectomy blocks or cuts the vas deferens.
